The Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on Surah 20, verses 39–40 (part 1 of 2):

The interpretation (ta'wil) of His words, exalted is He: ﴿Throw him into the chest, then throw it into the river, and the river will cast it onto the bank, and there will take him an enemy of Mine and an enemy of his. And I cast upon you love from Me﴾ [20:39].

He, exalted is His remembrance, says: And We had already bestowed favour upon you, O Musa, another time, when We inspired your mother, that throw your son Musa, when you gave birth to him, into the chest. ﴿Then throw him into the river﴾, meaning by the river the Nile. ﴿Then the river will cast him onto the bank﴾: that is, throw him into the river, and the river will cast him onto the bank. This is a conditional clause given in the form of a command, as though the river were the one being commanded, just as He, exalted is His praise, said: ﴿Follow our way, and we will bear your sins﴾ [29:12], meaning: follow our way and we will bear your sins for you. So his mother did this, and the river cast him at the landing place of the family of Pharaoh.

As related:

⁕ Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Salamah narrated to us, from Ibn Ishaq, who said: When Musa's mother gave birth to him, she nursed him. Then, when Pharaoh ordered the slaughter of the newborn boys of that year, she resorted to him and did with him what God the Exalted had commanded her. She placed him in a small chest, and she prepared a bed for him within it. Then she went to the Nile and cast him into it. Pharaoh awoke in a gathering he used to hold on the bank of the Nile every morning. While he was sitting there, the Nile carried the chest and cast it forth, while Asiya, the daughter of Muzahim, his wife, was sitting beside him. He said: "Surely this is something in the sea; bring it to me." So his attendants went out until they brought it to him. They opened the chest, and there in it was a boy in his cradle. God put His love upon him, and He inclined his soul toward him. By His words, exalted is His praise, ﴿there will take him an enemy of Mine and an enemy of his﴾, He meant that Pharaoh is the enemy of God and of Musa.

⁕ Musa narrated to us, saying: 'Amr narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi, regarding His words ﴿Then throw him into the river﴾, that the river is the sea, which is the Nile.

The scholars of ta'wil differed regarding the meaning of the love that God, exalted is His praise, mentioned in His words ﴿And I cast upon you love from Me﴾. Some of them said: He means that He made him beloved to His servants.

Those who said this:

⁕ al-Husayn ibn 'Ali al-Sada'i and al-'Abbas ibn Muhammad al-Duri told me, both saying: Husayn al-Ju'fi narrated to us, from Musa ibn Qays al-Hadrami, from Salamah ibn Kuhayl, regarding the saying of God ﴿And I cast upon you love from Me﴾. Al-'Abbas said: "I made you beloved to My servants." Al-Sada'i said: "I made you beloved to My creation."

Others said: Rather, the meaning of that is: He made your form beautiful.

Those who said this:

⁕ al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Ibrahim ibn Mahdi related to me, from a man, from al-Hakam ibn Aban, from 'Ikrimah, regarding His saying ﴿And I cast upon you love from Me﴾: "Beauty and comeliness."

Abu Ja'far (al-Tabari) said: The view closest to correctness regarding this matter is to say that God cast His love upon Musa, as He, exalted is His praise, said: ﴿And I cast upon you love from Me﴾. So He made him beloved to Asiya, the wife of Pharaoh, until she adopted him, nourished him and raised him; and to Pharaoh, until he withheld from him his enmity and his evil. It has also been said: It is only said "And I cast upon you love from Me" because He made him beloved to everyone who saw him. The meaning of ﴿And I cast upon you love from Me﴾ is: I made you beloved to them. A man says to another when he loves him: "I cast upon you My mercy," meaning: My love.

"39"

* *

The interpretation of His words, exalted is He: ﴿And that you may be raised under My eye. When your sister walks and says: "Shall I direct you to one who will take charge of him?" So We returned you to your mother that her eye might be comforted and she would not grieve. And you killed a soul, but We delivered you from distress and tested you with a testing. Then you remained years among the people of Madyan. Then you came according to decree, O Musa﴾ [20:39–40].

The scholars of ta'wil differed regarding the interpretation of His words ﴿And that you may be raised under My eye﴾. Some of them said: its meaning is: that you may be nourished and raised with My love and My will.

Those who said this:

⁕ al-Hasan ibn Yahya narrated to us, saying: 'Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: He is his nourishment, and that he be nourished under My eye.

⁕ Yunus related to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His words ﴿And that you may be raised under My eye﴾: He placed him in the house of the king, where he was pampered and lived in luxury; his nourishment was the nourishment of kings. That is the "ṣun'ah" (raising/fashioning).

Others said: Rather, the meaning of that is: You are under My eye in all your circumstances.

Those who said this:

⁕ al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj related to me, from Ibn Jurayj, regarding ﴿And that you may be raised under My eye﴾: "You are under My eye when your mother placed you in the chest, then in the sea, and ﴿when your sister walks﴾." Ibn Nahik recited ﴿wa-litusna'a﴾ with a fatha on the ta' (wa-litaṣna'a).

And he interpreted it...

As related:

⁕ Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Yahya ibn Wadih narrated to us, saying: 'Abd al-Mu'min narrated to us, saying: I heard Abu Nahik reciting ﴿wa-litaṣna'a 'alā 'aynī﴾, so I asked him about it, and he said: "And that you may act under My eye."

Abu Ja'far (al-Tabari) said: The recitation (qira'ah) that I do not permit recitation other than is ﴿wa-litusna'a﴾ with a damma on the ta', because of the ijma' (consensus) of the authoritative reciters upon it.

Since that is the case, the most preferred of the two interpretations is the interpretation given by Qatadah, which is: ﴿And that you may be nourished under My eye﴾: "I cast upon you love from Me." By His words ﴿under My eye﴾ He means: in My sight, with My love and My will.

* *

As for His words ﴿When your sister walks and says: "Shall I direct you to one who will take charge of him?"﴾:

He, exalted is His remembrance, says: When your sister walked, following you until she found you, then she went to those seeking wet-nurses for you and said: "Shall I direct you to one who will take charge of him?" The words after ﴿When your sister walks﴾ have been omitted, being understood from the context.

The sister of Musa said that to them because of what:

⁕ Musa ibn Harun narrated to us, saying: 'Amr narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi, who said: When his mother cast him into the sea, ﴿she said to his sister: "Follow him"﴾ [28:11]. When the family of Pharaoh picked him up, they sought wet-nurses for him, but he would not take from any of the women. The women began seeking that, so that they might gain a position with Pharaoh through nursing him, but he refused to take anyone. His sister said: ﴿Shall I direct you to a household who will take charge of him for you, and who will be sincere to him?﴾ So they seized her and said: "Rather, you know this boy, so direct us to his family." She said: "I do not know him, but I only said that they are sincere to the king."

⁕ Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Salamah narrated to us, from Ibn Ishaq, who said: She, meaning Musa's mother, said to his sister: "Follow him, and see what they do with him." So she went out for that, ﴿and she observed him from afar while they did not perceive﴾ [28:11]. He had come to need nursing and sought the breast, and they gathered wet-nurses for him when God cast their affection upon him. But no woman would be brought whose breast he would accept, which would distress them, so a wet-nurse would be brought after another wet-nurse, and he would not accept any of them. His sister said to them, seeing their concern for him and their eagerness for him: ﴿Shall I direct you to a household who will take charge of him for you, and who will be sincere to him?﴾ That is, because of his standing with you and your eagerness to please the king. By His words ﴿Shall I direct you to one who will take charge of him?﴾ He meant: Shall I direct you to one who will take him to themselves, guard him, nurse him and raise him? It has been said: the meaning of ﴿and He made Zakariyya his guardian﴾ [3:37] is that he took her in.

* *

As for His words ﴿So We returned you to your mother that her eye might be comforted and she would not grieve﴾:

He, exalted is His remembrance, says: We returned you to your mother after you had come into the hands of the family of Pharaoh, so that her eye would be comforted by your safety and your deliverance from being killed and from drowning in the sea, and so that she would not grieve over you out of fear for you from Pharaoh, lest he kill you.

As related:

⁕ Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Salamah narrated to us, from Ibn Ishaq, who said: When Musa's sister said to them what she said, they said: "Bring her." So she went to his mother and informed her, and she set off with her until they reached them. They handed him to her, and when she placed him in her lap, he took her breast, and they rejoiced at that from him. God returned him to his mother so that her eye would be comforted and she would not grieve. The kindness of God toward her and toward him reached the point that He returned her son to her, and the benefit of Pharaoh and the people of his household inclined toward her, together with safety from the killing that was feared for others. It was as though they were from the household of Pharaoh in safety and ease, and he was upon the carpets and thrones of Pharaoh.

* *

As for His words ﴿And you killed a soul﴾:

He, exalted is His praise, means by this: the Coptic man whom he killed, when the Israelite called on him for help against him, so Musa struck him.

* *

As for His words ﴿but We delivered you from distress﴾:

He, exalted is His remembrance, says: We delivered you from your distress caused by killing the soul you killed, when they wanted to kill you in retaliation for it, and We rescued you from them, until you fled to the people of Madyan, and they could not reach you to kill you in retaliation.

His killing of him, as has been mentioned, was an error,

as related:

⁕ Wasil ibn 'Abd al-A'la narrated to me, saying: Muhammad ibn Fudayl narrated to us, from his father, from Salim, from 'Abdullah ibn 'Umar, who said: I heard the Messenger of God (ﷺ) say: "Musa only killed the one he killed from the family of Pharaoh by mistake, so God said to him: ﴿And you killed a soul, but We delivered you from distress and tested you with a testing﴾."

⁕ Zakariyya ibn Yahya ibn Abi Za'idah and Muhammad ibn 'Amr related to me, both saying: Abu 'Asim narrated to us, saying: 'Isa narrated to us, and al-Harith related to me, saying: al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Warqa' narrated to us, all from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding ﴿but We delivered you from distress﴾: "From killing the soul."

⁕ Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding ﴿but We delivered you from distress﴾: "The soul that he killed."

The scholars of ta'wil differed regarding the interpretation of His words ﴿and tested you with a testing﴾. Some of them said: We tried you with a trial and tested you with a test.

Those who said this:

⁕ 'Ali related to me, saying: 'Abdullah narrated to us, saying: Mu'awiyah related to me, from 'Ali, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding His words ﴿and tested you with a testing﴾: He says, "We tested you with a test."

⁕ Muhammad ibn Sa'd related to me, saying: My father related to me, saying: My paternal uncle related to me, saying: My father related to me, from his father, from Ibn 'Abbas, ﴿and tested you with a testing﴾: "You were afflicted with an affliction."

⁕ al-'Abbas ibn al-Walid al-Amili related to me, saying: Yazid ibn Harun narrated to us, saying: Asbagh ibn Zayd al-Juhani informed us, saying: al-Qasim ibn Ayyub informed us, saying: Sa'id ibn Jubayr related to me, who said: I asked 'Abdullah ibn 'Abbas about the saying of God to Musa, ﴿and tested you with a testing﴾, and I asked him: "What is the fitnah (trial)?" He said to me: "Begin the day, O Ibn Jubayr, for it has a long narrative." He said: When I arose in the morning, I went early to Ibn 'Abbas to receive from him what he had promised me. He said: Pharaoh and his companions discussed what God had promised Ibrahim, that He would place among his descendants prophets and kings. Some of them said: The Children of Israel are awaiting that and are not doubtful of it, and they used to think that it was Yusuf ibn Ya'qub. When he died, they said: "God did not promise Ibrahim in this way." Pharaoh said: "Then what do you think?" He said: They consulted among themselves and resolved to send men with knives who would go around among the Children of Israel, and they would not find a male child without slaughtering him. When they saw that the elders of the Children of Israel were dying of their natural ends, and that the young were being slaughtered, they said: "The Children of Israel will soon be wiped out, and you will be left to do the work and service that they used to perform for you. So kill every male child for one year, and it will reduce their children. Leave one year in which you kill none of them, so that the young will grow up in place of those of them who die, for they will not multiply through those you spare, and you will not fear their increase over you, nor will they decrease through those you kill." They resolved upon that.

Musa's mother became pregnant with Harun in the following year, when boys were not slaughtered, and she gave birth to him openly and safely. Then, when the following year came, she became pregnant with Musa, and anxiety and grief entered her heart. That was part of the fitnah, O Ibn Jubayr, that entered upon him in his mother's womb, of what was intended for him. God inspired her: ﴿Do not fear and do not grieve. Indeed, We will return him to you and make him among the messengers﴾ [28:7]. He commanded her that when she gave birth to him, she should place him in a chest and then cast him into the sea. When she gave birth to him, she did what she had been commanded, until her son disappeared from her. Then Iblis came to her, and she said to herself: "What would I have done with my son if he had been slaughtered before me? I would have buried him and shrouded him, which would have been dearer to me than casting him by my own hand to the fish of the sea and its creatures." So the water carried him until it brought him to the landing place where the maidservants of the family of Pharaoh drew water. They saw him and took him, and they intended to open the chest. But one of them said to the others: "In this there is wealth, and if we open it, the wife of Pharaoh will not believe us about what we found in it." So they carried it as it was, without moving anything in it, until they handed it to her. When she opened it, she saw the boy in it, and love for him was cast upon her, such that she had never felt the like of it for anyone. ﴿And the heart of Musa's mother became empty﴾ [28:10] of everything except remembrance of Musa. When the slaughterers heard of his matter, they came to the wife of Pharaoh with their knives, wanting to slaughter him. That was part of the fitnah, O Ibn Jubayr. She said to the slaughterers: "Go away from me, for this one will not add to the Children of Israel. I will go to Pharaoh and ask him to grant him to me. If he grants him to me, you will have done well and beautifully, and if he orders his slaughter, I will not blame you." When she brought him to Pharaoh, she said: ﴿A comfort of the eye for me and for you﴾ [28:9]. Pharaoh said: "He will be yours, but as for me, I have no need of him." He said: By the One by Whom one swears, if Pharaoh had acknowledged that he would be a comfort of the eye for him as she did, God would have guided him through him, as He guided his wife through him. But God denied him that. She sent for every woman around her who had milk, to choose a nurse for him. Every time a woman from among them took him to nurse him, he would not accept her breast, until the wife of Pharaoh feared that he would refuse milk and die, and that grieved her. She commanded that he be taken out to the market, the gathering place of people, hoping to find a nurse from whom he would take. But he did not accept from anyone. Musa's mother awoke and said to his sister: "Follow him and search for him, and see whether you hear any mention of him, whether my son is alive, or whether the creatures of the sea and its fish have eaten him." She had forgotten what God had promised her. His sister observed him from afar while they did not perceive, and out of joy, when they had tired of the rounds of nurses, she said: "I will direct you to a household who will take charge of him for you, and who will be sincere to him." They seized her and said: "What do you know of their sincerity toward him? Do they know him, so that they could be suspicious of this?" That was part of the fitnah, O Ibn Jubayr. She said: "Their sincerity toward him and their compassion for him is their desire for the king's favour and their hope for his benefit." So they left her alone. She went to her mother and informed her of the news, and she came. When she placed him in her lap, he leaned toward her breast until both his sides were filled. The messengers went to the wife of Pharaoh to give her good news: "We have found a nurse for your son." She sent for her, and she was brought with him. When she saw what he was doing with her, she said: "Stay with me until you nurse this son of mine, for I have never loved anything as I love his love." She said: "I cannot leave my house and my child, for he would be lost. If it pleases you to give him to me, I will take him to my house, and he will be with me, and I will spare nothing good for him. If not, I will not leave my house and my child." Musa's mother recalled what God had promised her. She refused the wife of Pharaoh, and she was certain that God, blessed and exalted, would fulfil His promise. So she returned with her son to her house that very day. God caused him to grow well, and He preserved him for what He had decreed for him. The Children of Israel never ceased, gathered in a district of the city, protecting themselves through him from the oppression and the forced labour that were imposed upon them.

When the boy grew up, Pharaoh's wife said to Moses' mother: "Let me see my son." She had promised her a day on which she would show him to her. She then said to her attendants, eunuchs and servants: "None of you should be left without going out to meet my son with a gift and an honour, so that he may see it. I am sending a trustworthy person to count everything each of you does." The gifts, honours and presents kept meeting him from the moment he left his mother's house until he entered upon Pharaoh's wife. When he entered upon her, she bestowed gifts on him, honoured him, and rejoiced in him, and she was pleased by the good effect she saw of her upbringing of him. She said: "Take him to Pharaoh, so that he may bestow gifts on him and honour him." When they brought him to him, she placed him on her lap, and Moses took hold of Pharaoh's beard and pulled it. An enemy of the enemies of God said: "Do you not see what God promised Abraham, that he would overthrow you and overpower you?" So he sent for the executioners to slaughter him. That was among the trials, O son of Jubayr, after every affliction with which he was tested and which was intended for him. Then Pharaoh's wife came running to Pharaoh and said: "What has come over you concerning this boy whom I have given to me?" He said: "Do you not see that he claims he will overthrow me and overpower me?" She said: "Set between you and him a test by which you will know the truth. Bring two embers and two pearls, and bring them near to him. If he reaches for the two pearls and avoids the two embers, you will know that he understands. But if he takes the two embers and does not desire the two pearls, then know that no one who has understanding prefers the embers to the pearls." They brought that near to him, and he took the two embers, so they took them from him, fearing they would burn his hand. The woman said: "Do you not see?" So God turned him away from it after he had intended it, for God accomplishes His command.

When he reached his maturity and became a man, no one from the household of Pharaoh could reach any of the Children of Israel with him through oppression or forced labour, until they were thoroughly restrained. Then one day, while he was walking in a part of the city, he came upon two men fighting, one of them from the Children of Israel and the other from the household of Pharaoh. The Israelite called on him for help against the Egyptian, so Moses became angry and his anger intensified, because the man had attacked him while knowing Moses' position among the Children of Israel and his protection of them. People did not know anything except that this was due to his nursing by someone other than Moses' mother, unless God had informed Moses of something of that which no one else had been informed. So Moses struck the Egyptian and killed him, and no one saw them except God and the Israelite. Moses said, when he had killed the man: "This is from the work of Satan; indeed, he is an open, misleading enemy." Then he said: "My Lord, I have wronged myself, so forgive me," and He forgave him; indeed, He is the Forgiving, the Merciful. "So he woke up in the city, fearful and watchful" (Qur'an 28:18). The news spread. He went to Pharaoh, and it was said to him: "The Children of Israel have killed a man from the household of Pharaoh; so take our right from them and do not give them leave in this." He said: "Bring me his killer and someone who will testify against him, for it is not proper for me to judge without evidence or proof." They sought that, but while they were searching and could not find any proof, Moses passed by the next day and saw that Israelite fighting an Egyptian. The Israelite called on him for help against the Egyptian. Moses met him after he had regretted what he had done the day before and disliked what he had seen. Moses became angry, stretched out his hand, intending to strike the Egyptian. He said to the Israelite, because of what he had done yesterday and today: "Indeed, you are clearly an error-maker" (Qur'an 28:18). After he had spoken, the Israelite looked at Moses and saw that he was angry, as he had been angry the day before when he killed the Egyptian. He feared that, after he had said to him "Indeed, you are clearly an error-maker," Moses might have intended him, though he had not intended him but only the Egyptian. So the Israelite became fearful, and he restrained the Egyptian, saying: "O Moses, do you intend to kill me as you killed a soul yesterday?" (Qur'an 28:19). He said that only out of fear that Moses intended to kill him, so they separated. The Egyptian went to his people and told them what he had heard from the Israelite, namely: "Do you intend to kill me as you killed a soul yesterday?" Pharaoh then sent the executioners, and Moses took the main road, so they searched for him, not fearing that they would miss him. A man from Moses' party came from the far end of the city, took a short cut, and reached Moses before them, and informed him of the news. That was among the trials, O son of Jubayr.

Ibn Abi Najih reported from Mujahid, regarding His words "tests" (Qur'an 20:40): he said: "Affliction: His being placed in the chest, then in the sea, then the family of Pharaoh picking him up, then his going out fearful." (Muhammad ibn Amr said: Abu 'Asim said: "fearful" or "hungry" (Abu 'Asim doubted), and al-Harith said: "fearful, watchful," and he did not doubt.)

Al-Qasim reported to us: al-Husayn told us: Hajjaj told me, from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujahid, the same, and said: "fearful, watchful," and he did not doubt.

Bishr reported to us: Yazid told us: Sa'id reported to us, from Qatada, regarding His words "And We tested you with a testing" (Qur'an 20:40), he said: "We afflicted you with an affliction."

It was reported to me from al-Husayn, who said: I heard Abu Mu'adh say: 'Ubayd informed us, who said: I heard al-Dahhak say regarding His words "And We tested you with a testing" (Qur'an 20:40): it is affliction following affliction.

Others said: the meaning of that is: "We purified you."

Those who said that:

Al-Harith reported to me: al-Hasan told us: Waraqa told us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding "And We tested you with a testing" (Qur'an 20:40): "We purified you with purification."

Ibn al-Muthanna reported to us: Muhammad ibn Ja'far told us: Shu'ba told us, from Ya'la ibn Muslim, who said: I heard Sa'id ibn Jubayr explaining this word, "And We tested you with a testing" (Qur'an 20:40), and he said: "We purified you with purification."

Abu Ja'far (al-Tabari) said: We have already explained earlier in this book the meaning of fitna (trial, a test), that it is affliction and examination through proofs that make repetition here unnecessary.

* *

As for His words, "Then you remained for years among the people of Madyan" (Qur'an 20:40):

This statement omits part of what is needed for its completion, being sufficient by what is indicated of what was omitted. The meaning of the statement is: "And We tested you with a testing," so you went out fearful to the people of Madyan, and you remained among them for years.

* *

As for His words, "Then you came at the appointed time, O Moses" (Qur'an 20:40):

He, may His praise be exalted, says: Then you came at the appointed time at which We intended to send you to Pharaoh as a messenger, and at its measure.

The exegetes said things similar to what we have said about it.

Those who said that:

Muhammad ibn Sa'd reported to me: my father told me: my uncle told me: my father told me, from his father, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding His words "Then you came at the appointed time, O Moses" (Qur'an 20:40), he said: "You came at the appointed time, O Moses."

Muhammad ibn Amr reported to me: Abu 'Asim told us: 'Isa told us; and al-Harith told me: al-Hasan told us: Waraqa told us, all from Mujahid, who said regarding "at an appointed measure, O Moses" (Qur'an 20:40): "an appointment."

al-Qasim reported to us: al-Husayn told us: Hajjaj told me, from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujahid, who said: "according to an appointed time."

al-Hasan ibn Yahya reported to us: 'Abd al-Razzaq informed us: Ma'mar informed us, from Qatada, regarding His words "at an appointed measure, O Moses" (Qur'an 20:40): "the measure of the message and prophethood." The Arabs say: "So-and-so came at a measure," when he came at the appointed time of need for him; and from it is the poet's saying:

He attained the caliphate, or it was for him a measure,
as Moses came to his Lord at a measure. [This verse is by Jarir, from a poem of twenty-nine verses in his Diwan (Sawi edition, Cairo, pp. 274–276); the version there is "attained the caliphate," as in the author's version, and in some anthologies of evidence it is "came to the caliphate." In the margin of the Diwan: it is also narrated as "honoured the caliphate." The point of evidence in the verse is his saying "at a measure," meaning: the decreed fitting time. Al-Lisan (under q-d-r) says: one says "God decreed such a thing, a decree," and when a thing matches another thing one says "its measure came"; Ibn Sida said: qadr and qadar (with the letter dal vowelled or unvowelled) mean decree and judgment, which is what God, may He be exalted, decrees of matters and judges concerning them.]

The Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on Surah 20, verses 39–40 (part 1 of 2):

The interpretation (ta'wil) of His words, exalted is He: ﴿Throw him into the chest, then throw it into the river, and the river will cast it onto the bank, and there will take him an enemy of Mine and an enemy of his. And I cast upon you love from Me﴾ [20:39].

He, exalted is His remembrance, says: And We had already bestowed favour upon you, O Musa, another time, when We inspired your mother, that throw your son Musa, when you gave birth to him, into the chest. ﴿Then throw him into the river﴾, meaning by the river the Nile. ﴿Then the river will cast him onto the bank﴾: that is, throw him into the river, and the river will cast him onto the bank. This is a conditional clause given in the form of a command, as though the river were the one being commanded, just as He, exalted is His praise, said: ﴿Follow our way, and we will bear your sins﴾ [29:12], meaning: follow our way and we will bear your sins for you. So his mother did this, and the river cast him at the landing place of the family of Pharaoh.

As related:

⁕ Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Salamah narrated to us, from Ibn Ishaq, who said: When Musa's mother gave birth to him, she nursed him. Then, when Pharaoh ordered the slaughter of the newborn boys of that year, she resorted to him and did with him what God the Exalted had commanded her. She placed him in a small chest, and she prepared a bed for him within it. Then she went to the Nile and cast him into it. Pharaoh awoke in a gathering he used to hold on the bank of the Nile every morning. While he was sitting there, the Nile carried the chest and cast it forth, while Asiya, the daughter of Muzahim, his wife, was sitting beside him. He said: "Surely this is something in the sea; bring it to me." So his attendants went out until they brought it to him. They opened the chest, and there in it was a boy in his cradle. God put His love upon him, and He inclined his soul toward him. By His words, exalted is His praise, ﴿there will take him an enemy of Mine and an enemy of his﴾, He meant that Pharaoh is the enemy of God and of Musa.

⁕ Musa narrated to us, saying: 'Amr narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi, regarding His words ﴿Then throw him into the river﴾, that the river is the sea, which is the Nile.

The scholars of ta'wil differed regarding the meaning of the love that God, exalted is His praise, mentioned in His words ﴿And I cast upon you love from Me﴾. Some of them said: He means that He made him beloved to His servants.

Those who said this:

⁕ al-Husayn ibn 'Ali al-Sada'i and al-'Abbas ibn Muhammad al-Duri told me, both saying: Husayn al-Ju'fi narrated to us, from Musa ibn Qays al-Hadrami, from Salamah ibn Kuhayl, regarding the saying of God ﴿And I cast upon you love from Me﴾. Al-'Abbas said: "I made you beloved to My servants." Al-Sada'i said: "I made you beloved to My creation."

Others said: Rather, the meaning of that is: He made your form beautiful.

Those who said this:

⁕ al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Ibrahim ibn Mahdi related to me, from a man, from al-Hakam ibn Aban, from 'Ikrimah, regarding His saying ﴿And I cast upon you love from Me﴾: "Beauty and comeliness."

Abu Ja'far (al-Tabari) said: The view closest to correctness regarding this matter is to say that God cast His love upon Musa, as He, exalted is His praise, said: ﴿And I cast upon you love from Me﴾. So He made him beloved to Asiya, the wife of Pharaoh, until she adopted him, nourished him and raised him; and to Pharaoh, until he withheld from him his enmity and his evil. It has also been said: It is only said "And I cast upon you love from Me" because He made him beloved to everyone who saw him. The meaning of ﴿And I cast upon you love from Me﴾ is: I made you beloved to them. A man says to another when he loves him: "I cast upon you My mercy," meaning: My love.

"39"

* *

The interpretation of His words, exalted is He: ﴿And that you may be raised under My eye. When your sister walks and says: "Shall I direct you to one who will take charge of him?" So We returned you to your mother that her eye might be comforted and she would not grieve. And you killed a soul, but We delivered you from distress and tested you with a testing. Then you remained years among the people of Madyan. Then you came according to decree, O Musa﴾ [20:39–40].

The scholars of ta'wil differed regarding the interpretation of His words ﴿And that you may be raised under My eye﴾. Some of them said: its meaning is: that you may be nourished and raised with My love and My will.

Those who said this:

⁕ al-Hasan ibn Yahya narrated to us, saying: 'Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: He is his nourishment, and that he be nourished under My eye.

⁕ Yunus related to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His words ﴿And that you may be raised under My eye﴾: He placed him in the house of the king, where he was pampered and lived in luxury; his nourishment was the nourishment of kings. That is the "ṣun'ah" (raising/fashioning).

Others said: Rather, the meaning of that is: You are under My eye in all your circumstances.

Those who said this:

⁕ al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj related to me, from Ibn Jurayj, regarding ﴿And that you may be raised under My eye﴾: "You are under My eye when your mother placed you in the chest, then in the sea, and ﴿when your sister walks﴾." Ibn Nahik recited ﴿wa-litusna'a﴾ with a fatha on the ta' (wa-litaṣna'a).

And he interpreted it...

As related:

⁕ Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Yahya ibn Wadih narrated to us, saying: 'Abd al-Mu'min narrated to us, saying: I heard Abu Nahik reciting ﴿wa-litaṣna'a 'alā 'aynī﴾, so I asked him about it, and he said: "And that you may act under My eye."

Abu Ja'far (al-Tabari) said: The recitation (qira'ah) that I do not permit recitation other than is ﴿wa-litusna'a﴾ with a damma on the ta', because of the ijma' (consensus) of the authoritative reciters upon it.

Since that is the case, the most preferred of the two interpretations is the interpretation given by Qatadah, which is: ﴿And that you may be nourished under My eye﴾: "I cast upon you love from Me." By His words ﴿under My eye﴾ He means: in My sight, with My love and My will.

* *

As for His words ﴿When your sister walks and says: "Shall I direct you to one who will take charge of him?"﴾:

He, exalted is His remembrance, says: When your sister walked, following you until she found you, then she went to those seeking wet-nurses for you and said: "Shall I direct you to one who will take charge of him?" The words after ﴿When your sister walks﴾ have been omitted, being understood from the context.

The sister of Musa said that to them because of what:

⁕ Musa ibn Harun narrated to us, saying: 'Amr narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi, who said: When his mother cast him into the sea, ﴿she said to his sister: "Follow him"﴾ [28:11]. When the family of Pharaoh picked him up, they sought wet-nurses for him, but he would not take from any of the women. The women began seeking that, so that they might gain a position with Pharaoh through nursing him, but he refused to take anyone. His sister said: ﴿Shall I direct you to a household who will take charge of him for you, and who will be sincere to him?﴾ So they seized her and said: "Rather, you know this boy, so direct us to his family." She said: "I do not know him, but I only said that they are sincere to the king."

⁕ Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Salamah narrated to us, from Ibn Ishaq, who said: She, meaning Musa's mother, said to his sister: "Follow him, and see what they do with him." So she went out for that, ﴿and she observed him from afar while they did not perceive﴾ [28:11]. He had come to need nursing and sought the breast, and they gathered wet-nurses for him when God cast their affection upon him. But no woman would be brought whose breast he would accept, which would distress them, so a wet-nurse would be brought after another wet-nurse, and he would not accept any of them. His sister said to them, seeing their concern for him and their eagerness for him: ﴿Shall I direct you to a household who will take charge of him for you, and who will be sincere to him?﴾ That is, because of his standing with you and your eagerness to please the king. By His words ﴿Shall I direct you to one who will take charge of him?﴾ He meant: Shall I direct you to one who will take him to themselves, guard him, nurse him and raise him? It has been said: the meaning of ﴿and He made Zakariyya his guardian﴾ [3:37] is that he took her in.

* *

As for His words ﴿So We returned you to your mother that her eye might be comforted and she would not grieve﴾:

He, exalted is His remembrance, says: We returned you to your mother after you had come into the hands of the family of Pharaoh, so that her eye would be comforted by your safety and your deliverance from being killed and from drowning in the sea, and so that she would not grieve over you out of fear for you from Pharaoh, lest he kill you.

As related:

⁕ Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Salamah narrated to us, from Ibn Ishaq, who said: When Musa's sister said to them what she said, they said: "Bring her." So she went to his mother and informed her, and she set off with her until they reached them. They handed him to her, and when she placed him in her lap, he took her breast, and they rejoiced at that from him. God returned him to his mother so that her eye would be comforted and she would not grieve. The kindness of God toward her and toward him reached the point that He returned her son to her, and the benefit of Pharaoh and the people of his household inclined toward her, together with safety from the killing that was feared for others. It was as though they were from the household of Pharaoh in safety and ease, and he was upon the carpets and thrones of Pharaoh.

* *

As for His words ﴿And you killed a soul﴾:

He, exalted is His praise, means by this: the Coptic man whom he killed, when the Israelite called on him for help against him, so Musa struck him.

* *

As for His words ﴿but We delivered you from distress﴾:

He, exalted is His remembrance, says: We delivered you from your distress caused by killing the soul you killed, when they wanted to kill you in retaliation for it, and We rescued you from them, until you fled to the people of Madyan, and they could not reach you to kill you in retaliation.

His killing of him, as has been mentioned, was an error,

as related:

⁕ Wasil ibn 'Abd al-A'la narrated to me, saying: Muhammad ibn Fudayl narrated to us, from his father, from Salim, from 'Abdullah ibn 'Umar, who said: I heard the Messenger of God (ﷺ) say: "Musa only killed the one he killed from the family of Pharaoh by mistake, so God said to him: ﴿And you killed a soul, but We delivered you from distress and tested you with a testing﴾."

⁕ Zakariyya ibn Yahya ibn Abi Za'idah and Muhammad ibn 'Amr related to me, both saying: Abu 'Asim narrated to us, saying: 'Isa narrated to us, and al-Harith related to me, saying: al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Warqa' narrated to us, all from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding ﴿but We delivered you from distress﴾: "From killing the soul."

⁕ Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding ﴿but We delivered you from distress﴾: "The soul that he killed."

The scholars of ta'wil differed regarding the interpretation of His words ﴿and tested you with a testing﴾. Some of them said: We tried you with a trial and tested you with a test.

Those who said this:

⁕ 'Ali related to me, saying: 'Abdullah narrated to us, saying: Mu'awiyah related to me, from 'Ali, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding His words ﴿and tested you with a testing﴾: He says, "We tested you with a test."

⁕ Muhammad ibn Sa'd related to me, saying: My father related to me, saying: My paternal uncle related to me, saying: My father related to me, from his father, from Ibn 'Abbas, ﴿and tested you with a testing﴾: "You were afflicted with an affliction."

⁕ al-'Abbas ibn al-Walid al-Amili related to me, saying: Yazid ibn Harun narrated to us, saying: Asbagh ibn Zayd al-Juhani informed us, saying: al-Qasim ibn Ayyub informed us, saying: Sa'id ibn Jubayr related to me, who said: I asked 'Abdullah ibn 'Abbas about the saying of God to Musa, ﴿and tested you with a testing﴾, and I asked him: "What is the fitnah (trial)?" He said to me: "Begin the day, O Ibn Jubayr, for it has a long narrative." He said: When I arose in the morning, I went early to Ibn 'Abbas to receive from him what he had promised me. He said: Pharaoh and his companions discussed what God had promised Ibrahim, that He would place among his descendants prophets and kings. Some of them said: The Children of Israel are awaiting that and are not doubtful of it, and they used to think that it was Yusuf ibn Ya'qub. When he died, they said: "God did not promise Ibrahim in this way." Pharaoh said: "Then what do you think?" He said: They consulted among themselves and resolved to send men with knives who would go around among the Children of Israel, and they would not find a male child without slaughtering him. When they saw that the elders of the Children of Israel were dying of their natural ends, and that the young were being slaughtered, they said: "The Children of Israel will soon be wiped out, and you will be left to do the work and service that they used to perform for you. So kill every male child for one year, and it will reduce their children. Leave one year in which you kill none of them, so that the young will grow up in place of those of them who die, for they will not multiply through those you spare, and you will not fear their increase over you, nor will they decrease through those you kill." They resolved upon that.

Musa's mother became pregnant with Harun in the following year, when boys were not slaughtered, and she gave birth to him openly and safely. Then, when the following year came, she became pregnant with Musa, and anxiety and grief entered her heart. That was part of the fitnah, O Ibn Jubayr, that entered upon him in his mother's womb, of what was intended for him. God inspired her: ﴿Do not fear and do not grieve. Indeed, We will return him to you and make him among the messengers﴾ [28:7]. He commanded her that when she gave birth to him, she should place him in a chest and then cast him into the sea. When she gave birth to him, she did what she had been commanded, until her son disappeared from her. Then Iblis came to her, and she said to herself: "What would I have done with my son if he had been slaughtered before me? I would have buried him and shrouded him, which would have been dearer to me than casting him by my own hand to the fish of the sea and its creatures." So the water carried him until it brought him to the landing place where the maidservants of the family of Pharaoh drew water. They saw him and took him, and they intended to open the chest. But one of them said to the others: "In this there is wealth, and if we open it, the wife of Pharaoh will not believe us about what we found in it." So they carried it as it was, without moving anything in it, until they handed it to her. When she opened it, she saw the boy in it, and love for him was cast upon her, such that she had never felt the like of it for anyone. ﴿And the heart of Musa's mother became empty﴾ [28:10] of everything except remembrance of Musa. When the slaughterers heard of his matter, they came to the wife of Pharaoh with their knives, wanting to slaughter him. That was part of the fitnah, O Ibn Jubayr. She said to the slaughterers: "Go away from me, for this one will not add to the Children of Israel. I will go to Pharaoh and ask him to grant him to me. If he grants him to me, you will have done well and beautifully, and if he orders his slaughter, I will not blame you." When she brought him to Pharaoh, she said: ﴿A comfort of the eye for me and for you﴾ [28:9]. Pharaoh said: "He will be yours, but as for me, I have no need of him." He said: By the One by Whom one swears, if Pharaoh had acknowledged that he would be a comfort of the eye for him as she did, God would have guided him through him, as He guided his wife through him. But God denied him that. She sent for every woman around her who had milk, to choose a nurse for him. Every time a woman from among them took him to nurse him, he would not accept her breast, until the wife of Pharaoh feared that he would refuse milk and die, and that grieved her. She commanded that he be taken out to the market, the gathering place of people, hoping to find a nurse from whom he would take. But he did not accept from anyone. Musa's mother awoke and said to his sister: "Follow him and search for him, and see whether you hear any mention of him, whether my son is alive, or whether the creatures of the sea and its fish have eaten him." She had forgotten what God had promised her. His sister observed him from afar while they did not perceive, and out of joy, when they had tired of the rounds of nurses, she said: "I will direct you to a household who will take charge of him for you, and who will be sincere to him." They seized her and said: "What do you know of their sincerity toward him? Do they know him, so that they could be suspicious of this?" That was part of the fitnah, O Ibn Jubayr. She said: "Their sincerity toward him and their compassion for him is their desire for the king's favour and their hope for his benefit." So they left her alone. She went to her mother and informed her of the news, and she came. When she placed him in her lap, he leaned toward her breast until both his sides were filled. The messengers went to the wife of Pharaoh to give her good news: "We have found a nurse for your son." She sent for her, and she was brought with him. When she saw what he was doing with her, she said: "Stay with me until you nurse this son of mine, for I have never loved anything as I love his love." She said: "I cannot leave my house and my child, for he would be lost. If it pleases you to give him to me, I will take him to my house, and he will be with me, and I will spare nothing good for him. If not, I will not leave my house and my child." Musa's mother recalled what God had promised her. She refused the wife of Pharaoh, and she was certain that God, blessed and exalted, would fulfil His promise. So she returned with her son to her house that very day. God caused him to grow well, and He preserved him for what He had decreed for him. The Children of Israel never ceased, gathered in a district of the city, protecting themselves through him from the oppression and the forced labour that were imposed upon them.

When the boy grew up, Pharaoh's wife said to Moses' mother: "Let me see my son." She had promised her a day on which she would show him to her. She then said to her attendants, eunuchs and servants: "None of you should be left without going out to meet my son with a gift and an honour, so that he may see it. I am sending a trustworthy person to count everything each of you does." The gifts, honours and presents kept meeting him from the moment he left his mother's house until he entered upon Pharaoh's wife. When he entered upon her, she bestowed gifts on him, honoured him, and rejoiced in him, and she was pleased by the good effect she saw of her upbringing of him. She said: "Take him to Pharaoh, so that he may bestow gifts on him and honour him." When they brought him to him, she placed him on her lap, and Moses took hold of Pharaoh's beard and pulled it. An enemy of the enemies of God said: "Do you not see what God promised Abraham, that he would overthrow you and overpower you?" So he sent for the executioners to slaughter him. That was among the trials, O son of Jubayr, after every affliction with which he was tested and which was intended for him. Then Pharaoh's wife came running to Pharaoh and said: "What has come over you concerning this boy whom I have given to me?" He said: "Do you not see that he claims he will overthrow me and overpower me?" She said: "Set between you and him a test by which you will know the truth. Bring two embers and two pearls, and bring them near to him. If he reaches for the two pearls and avoids the two embers, you will know that he understands. But if he takes the two embers and does not desire the two pearls, then know that no one who has understanding prefers the embers to the pearls." They brought that near to him, and he took the two embers, so they took them from him, fearing they would burn his hand. The woman said: "Do you not see?" So God turned him away from it after he had intended it, for God accomplishes His command.

When he reached his maturity and became a man, no one from the household of Pharaoh could reach any of the Children of Israel with him through oppression or forced labour, until they were thoroughly restrained. Then one day, while he was walking in a part of the city, he came upon two men fighting, one of them from the Children of Israel and the other from the household of Pharaoh. The Israelite called on him for help against the Egyptian, so Moses became angry and his anger intensified, because the man had attacked him while knowing Moses' position among the Children of Israel and his protection of them. People did not know anything except that this was due to his nursing by someone other than Moses' mother, unless God had informed Moses of something of that which no one else had been informed. So Moses struck the Egyptian and killed him, and no one saw them except God and the Israelite. Moses said, when he had killed the man: "This is from the work of Satan; indeed, he is an open, misleading enemy." Then he said: "My Lord, I have wronged myself, so forgive me," and He forgave him; indeed, He is the Forgiving, the Merciful. "So he woke up in the city, fearful and watchful" (Qur'an 28:18). The news spread. He went to Pharaoh, and it was said to him: "The Children of Israel have killed a man from the household of Pharaoh; so take our right from them and do not give them leave in this." He said: "Bring me his killer and someone who will testify against him, for it is not proper for me to judge without evidence or proof." They sought that, but while they were searching and could not find any proof, Moses passed by the next day and saw that Israelite fighting an Egyptian. The Israelite called on him for help against the Egyptian. Moses met him after he had regretted what he had done the day before and disliked what he had seen. Moses became angry, stretched out his hand, intending to strike the Egyptian. He said to the Israelite, because of what he had done yesterday and today: "Indeed, you are clearly an error-maker" (Qur'an 28:18). After he had spoken, the Israelite looked at Moses and saw that he was angry, as he had been angry the day before when he killed the Egyptian. He feared that, after he had said to him "Indeed, you are clearly an error-maker," Moses might have intended him, though he had not intended him but only the Egyptian. So the Israelite became fearful, and he restrained the Egyptian, saying: "O Moses, do you intend to kill me as you killed a soul yesterday?" (Qur'an 28:19). He said that only out of fear that Moses intended to kill him, so they separated. The Egyptian went to his people and told them what he had heard from the Israelite, namely: "Do you intend to kill me as you killed a soul yesterday?" Pharaoh then sent the executioners, and Moses took the main road, so they searched for him, not fearing that they would miss him. A man from Moses' party came from the far end of the city, took a short cut, and reached Moses before them, and informed him of the news. That was among the trials, O son of Jubayr.

Ibn Abi Najih reported from Mujahid, regarding His words "tests" (Qur'an 20:40): he said: "Affliction: His being placed in the chest, then in the sea, then the family of Pharaoh picking him up, then his going out fearful." (Muhammad ibn Amr said: Abu 'Asim said: "fearful" or "hungry" (Abu 'Asim doubted), and al-Harith said: "fearful, watchful," and he did not doubt.)

Al-Qasim reported to us: al-Husayn told us: Hajjaj told me, from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujahid, the same, and said: "fearful, watchful," and he did not doubt.

Bishr reported to us: Yazid told us: Sa'id reported to us, from Qatada, regarding His words "And We tested you with a testing" (Qur'an 20:40), he said: "We afflicted you with an affliction."

It was reported to me from al-Husayn, who said: I heard Abu Mu'adh say: 'Ubayd informed us, who said: I heard al-Dahhak say regarding His words "And We tested you with a testing" (Qur'an 20:40): it is affliction following affliction.

Others said: the meaning of that is: "We purified you."

Those who said that:

Al-Harith reported to me: al-Hasan told us: Waraqa told us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding "And We tested you with a testing" (Qur'an 20:40): "We purified you with purification."

Ibn al-Muthanna reported to us: Muhammad ibn Ja'far told us: Shu'ba told us, from Ya'la ibn Muslim, who said: I heard Sa'id ibn Jubayr explaining this word, "And We tested you with a testing" (Qur'an 20:40), and he said: "We purified you with purification."

Abu Ja'far (al-Tabari) said: We have already explained earlier in this book the meaning of fitna (trial, a test), that it is affliction and examination through proofs that make repetition here unnecessary.

* *

As for His words, "Then you remained for years among the people of Madyan" (Qur'an 20:40):

This statement omits part of what is needed for its completion, being sufficient by what is indicated of what was omitted. The meaning of the statement is: "And We tested you with a testing," so you went out fearful to the people of Madyan, and you remained among them for years.

* *

As for His words, "Then you came at the appointed time, O Moses" (Qur'an 20:40):

He, may His praise be exalted, says: Then you came at the appointed time at which We intended to send you to Pharaoh as a messenger, and at its measure.

The exegetes said things similar to what we have said about it.

Those who said that:

Muhammad ibn Sa'd reported to me: my father told me: my uncle told me: my father told me, from his father, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding His words "Then you came at the appointed time, O Moses" (Qur'an 20:40), he said: "You came at the appointed time, O Moses."

Muhammad ibn Amr reported to me: Abu 'Asim told us: 'Isa told us; and al-Harith told me: al-Hasan told us: Waraqa told us, all from Mujahid, who said regarding "at an appointed measure, O Moses" (Qur'an 20:40): "an appointment."

al-Qasim reported to us: al-Husayn told us: Hajjaj told me, from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujahid, who said: "according to an appointed time."

al-Hasan ibn Yahya reported to us: 'Abd al-Razzaq informed us: Ma'mar informed us, from Qatada, regarding His words "at an appointed measure, O Moses" (Qur'an 20:40): "the measure of the message and prophethood." The Arabs say: "So-and-so came at a measure," when he came at the appointed time of need for him; and from it is the poet's saying:

He attained the caliphate, or it was for him a measure,
as Moses came to his Lord at a measure. [This verse is by Jarir, from a poem of twenty-nine verses in his Diwan (Sawi edition, Cairo, pp. 274–276); the version there is "attained the caliphate," as in the author's version, and in some anthologies of evidence it is "came to the caliphate." In the margin of the Diwan: it is also narrated as "honoured the caliphate." The point of evidence in the verse is his saying "at a measure," meaning: the decreed fitting time. Al-Lisan (under q-d-r) says: one says "God decreed such a thing, a decree," and when a thing matches another thing one says "its measure came"; Ibn Sida said: qadr and qadar (with the letter dal vowelled or unvowelled) mean decree and judgment, which is what God, may He be exalted, decrees of matters and judges concerning them.]

The exegesis (al-Tabari's commentary, Jami al-Bayan) on Surah 20, verses 41–43:

On the interpretation (ta'wil) of His words, exalted is He: ﴿And I have chosen you for Myself﴾ [20:41] ﴿Go, you and your brother, with My signs, and do not slacken in remembering Me﴾ [20:42] ﴿Go, both of you, to Pharaoh; indeed, he has transgressed﴾ [20:43].

His exalted remembrance says: ﴿And I have chosen you for Myself﴾, meaning: I have bestowed upon you these blessings, O Musa, and conferred upon you these favours, choosing you from Me for yourself, and selecting you for My message, for conveying My word, and for carrying out My command and prohibition. ﴿Go, you and your brother﴾, Harun, ﴿with My signs﴾, meaning: with My proofs and My arguments. ﴿Go, both of you, to Pharaoh with them, for he has rebelled in his misguidance and transgression, so convey to him My messages.﴾ ﴿And do not slacken in remembering Me﴾, meaning: and do not weaken in remembering Me in what I have commanded and prohibited you. For your remembrance of Me strengthens your resolve and steadies your feet, because when you remember Me, you remember the many blessings and countless favours I have bestowed upon you. From this one says: "Fulan waniya fi hadha al-amr" and "'an hadha al-amr", meaning he weakened, and he yanī, waniyan, as al-'Ajjaj said:

"So Muhammad did not weaken since Allah forgave him what came before and what came after."

[These are two verses of rajaz (metre) (14, 15) from an urjuza of al-'Ajjaj (his Diwan, Leipzig edition, 1903, p. 15), and other variants. As in (Lisan al-Arab: w-n-y), al-fatra (lapse) in actions and affairs; wana yuni, wanyan and wunyan (on the pattern fu'ul), meaning he weakened. Tawanna fi hajatihi meant he fell short in his need. In a hadith of Aisha describing her father, may Allah be pleased with them both: "Sabaq, idha wanitum" (he preceded, when you slackened), meaning you fell short and lapsed.]

And in accordance with what we have said regarding this, the people of ta'wil (interpretation) have said.

Those who said so:

- Ali narrated to me, saying: Abdullah narrated to us, saying: Mu'awiya narrated to us, from Ali, from Ibn Abbas, regarding His words ﴿wa la tanyā﴾ (and do not slacken): he says, do not hesitate.

- Muhammad ibn Sa'd narrated to me, saying: my father narrated to me, saying: my paternal uncle narrated to me, saying: my father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn Abbas, regarding His words ﴿And do not slacken in remembering Me﴾: he says, do not weaken in remembering Me.

- Muhammad ibn Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu Asim narrated to us, saying: Isa narrated to us; and al-Harith narrated to me, saying: al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Warqa narrated to us, all from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His words ﴿And do not slacken in remembering Me﴾: he said, do not weaken.

- Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujahid, ﴿tanyā﴾: weaken.

- Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatada, regarding His words ﴿And do not slacken in remembering Me﴾: he says, do not weaken in remembering Me.

- al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Ma'mar informed us, from Qatada, regarding His words ﴿And do not slacken in remembering Me﴾: he said, do not weaken.

- It was related to me from al-Husayn, who said: I heard Abu Mu'adh say: Ubayd informed us, saying: I heard al-Dahhak say regarding His words ﴿And do not slacken in remembering Me﴾: he says, do not weaken.

- Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said regarding His words ﴿And do not slacken in remembering Me﴾: "al-wani" (the one who slackens) is the heedless one who is negligent in that.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 20, verses 44–45:

The interpretation of His saying, ﴿Speak to him gently, perhaps he will remember or fear﴾ (44) ﴿They said, "Our Lord, we fear that he will hasten against us or that he will transgress"﴾ (45).

He, may His remembrance be exalted, says to Moses and Aaron: "Speak to Pharaoh with gentle speech." It has been mentioned that the gentle speech which God commanded them to address to him was that they should address him by a kunya (kunya: an honorific nickname formed from "Abu" or "Umm").

⁕ Ja'far ibn Ibnat Ishaq ibn Yusuf al-Azraq narrated to me, saying: Sa'id ibn Muhammad al-Thaqafi narrated to us, saying: 'Ali ibn Salih narrated to us, from al-Suddi, regarding ﴿Speak to him gently﴾, he said: "They were to address him by his kunya."

* *

As for His saying ﴿perhaps he will remember or fear﴾:

Scholars differed about the meaning of His saying ﴿perhaps (la'alla)﴾ in this place. Some of them said its meaning here is interrogative, as if the sense of the speech was directed to: "Speak to him gently, and see whether he will remember and turn back, or fear God and desist from his transgression."

Mention of those who said this:

⁕ 'Ali narrated to me, saying: 'Abd Allah narrated to us, saying: Mu'awiya narrated to us, from 'Ali, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding His saying ﴿perhaps he will remember or fear﴾, he said: "Will he remember or fear?"

Others said: the meaning of la'alla here is "so that" (kay). They directed the sense of the speech to: (Go to Pharaoh, indeed he has transgressed), so that they should admonish him, "perhaps he will remember or fear," just as the speaker says: "Do your work, perhaps you will take your wage," meaning: so that you take your wage; and "Finish your work, perhaps we may have lunch," meaning: so that we may have lunch, or until we have lunch. Both of these opinions have a good sense and a sound approach.

* *

As for His saying ﴿They said, "Our Lord, we fear that he will hasten against us"﴾:

He, may His remembrance be exalted, says: Moses and Aaron said: "Our Lord, we fear Pharaoh, if we call him to what You have commanded us to call him to, that he will hasten to punish us." This is from the phrase "farata minni ila fulan amr," meaning: such a matter preceded from me to him. From it comes "fari' al-qawm," meaning the one who hurries ahead of them to the water or the resting place, as the rajiz said:

"The brute has hastened against us and rushed"[[In (al-Lisan: farata) "faraṭa 'alayhi yafrutu": he hurried against him and overpowered and harmed him. al-Farra' said regarding His saying (indeed we fear he will hasten against us): "he will hasten to our punishment." Al-'Ilj: a strong, large man. I did not know the author of the verse.]]

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 20, verse 51–52:

On the interpretation of His saying, exalted is His remembrance: ﴿Pharaoh said, "Then what about the former generations?" (51) [Moses] said, "Its knowledge is with my Lord, in a Book. My Lord neither errs nor forgets."﴾ (52) [Moses] said, "Its knowledge is with my Lord, in a Book. My Lord neither errs nor forgets."

He, exalted is His remembrance, says: Pharaoh said to Moses, when Moses described his Lord, exalted is His majesty, with what He was described with of great sovereignty and abundant bounty and favour toward His creatures: "What is the matter with the past nations before us, that they did not acknowledge what you say, did not believe in what you call to, and did not devote worship sincerely to Him, but worshipped gods and idols besides Him, if the matter is as you describe, that all things are His creation, and that they turn about in His blessings and move in His favours?" Moses answered him, saying: "The knowledge of those nations that passed before us regarding what they did in that matter is with my Lord, in a Book," meaning in the Mother of the Book. I have no knowledge of their affair, nor of the cause of the straying of those among them who went astray and departed from the religion of God. ﴿My Lord neither errs﴾ means: my Lord does not make a mistake in His management and His actions. So if He punished those generations swiftly and hastened their destruction, then what He did is right; and if He deferred their punishment until the Resurrection, then what He did is the truth, for He knows best what He does. My Lord does not err. ﴿Nor forgets﴾, so that He would leave off doing what He did, as wisdom and rightness require.

Tafsir scholars said what we have said on this matter.

Mention of those who said so:

- Ali related to me, saying: Abdullah told us, saying: Mu'awiyah related to me, from Ali, from Ibn Abbas, regarding His saying ﴿in a Book; my Lord neither errs nor forgets﴾: he said: my Lord does not make a mistake and does not forget.

So the Prophet of God entrusted it to a trusted deputy, and he said ﴿Its knowledge is with my Lord﴾ ... the verse; he said: that is, their lifespans and their appointed terms.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 20, verse 53:

The interpretation of His, the Exalted's, saying: ﴿Who made the earth for you a cradle and threaded for you therein roads and sent down from the sky water, and We brought forth thereby diverse kinds of plants﴾ (20:53).

The people of interpretation (ahl al-ta'wil) differed over the recitation of His saying ﴿mahdan﴾ (cradle). The majority of the reciters of Medina and Basra recited it ﴿Alladhi ja'ala lakumu al-ard mihadan﴾ (Who made the earth for you a bed), with a kasra on the mim, from al-mihad, and with an alif added after the ha', and their practice was the same throughout the Qur'an. Some who preferred this reading claimed that they chose it because al-mihad is a noun of place, whereas al-mahd is a verbal noun; he said it is like al-firash and al-faras. The majority of the reciters of Kufa recited it ﴿mahdan﴾, meaning: who made the earth a cradle for you.

The correct position on this is to say: both are widely transmitted readings, well known among the regional recitations, so whichever one the reciter reads, he is correct in it.

As for His saying ﴿wa-anzala mina al-sama'i ma'an﴾ (and sent down from the sky water):

He says: and sent down rain from the sky. ﴿Fa-akhrajna bihi azwajan min nabatin shatta﴾ (so We brought forth thereby diverse kinds of plants). This is a report from God, may His remembrance be exalted, about His bounty upon His creatures through the rain He sends down from His sky to His earth, after the conclusion of His report about Moses' answer to Pharaoh regarding what he asked him, and his praise of his Lord with what is worthy of Him. He, may His praise be glorified, says: So We brought forth, O people, by what We send down from the sky of water, pairs, meaning kinds of plants, diverse, meaning of differing tastes, scents, and appearances.

Similar to what we have said regarding this is what the people of interpretation have said.

Mentioning those who said this:

Ali narrated to me, saying: Abdullah narrated to us, saying: Mu'awiya narrated to me, from Ali, from Ibn Abbas, regarding His saying ﴿min nabatin shatta﴾: he said: diverse.

**The explanation of His words, may He be exalted: ﴿Eat and let your livestock graze. Indeed in that are signs for those of understanding﴾ (54)**

He, may His remembrance be exalted, says: Eat, O people, of the good things that We have brought forth for you by the rain that We sent down from the sky to the earth, of its fruits and its produce, which are your sustenance and nourishment. And let your livestock graze on what is their provision and sustenance from it. ﴿Indeed in that are signs﴾ means: indeed in what I have described in this verse of the power of your Lord and His great dominion are signs, meaning proofs and indications that point to the oneness of your Lord and that there is no god for you besides Him. ﴿For those of understanding﴾ means: for people of intellect and reason. *Al-nuha* (النُّهَى) is the plural of *nuhya* (نُهْيَة), just as *al-kusha* (الكُشَى) is the plural of *kushya* (كُشْيَة).

Abu Ja'far said: *Al-kusha* (الكُشَى) is a fatty substance found in the belly of the lizard (*dabb*), resembling the navel. God, may He be exalted, specified that these are signs for *ulu al-nuha* because they are people of reflection and consideration, and people of contemplation and admonition.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 20, verse 55–56:

The interpretation of His saying, ﴿From it We created you, and into it We will return you, and from it We will bring you out once more﴾ (55):

He, may His remembrance be exalted, says: From the earth We created you, O people, and then We brought you into being as embodied, speaking beings. ﴿And into it We will return you﴾ means: and into the earth We will return you after your deaths, so We will make you dust, just as you were before We brought you into being as a complete human. ﴿And from it We will bring you out﴾ means: and from the earth We will bring you out as you were before your deaths, alive, so We will produce you from it, just as We produced you the first time.

* *

And His saying ﴿once more﴾:

He says: a second time.

As related:

* Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding ﴿and from it We will bring you out once more﴾, he said: a second time.

* Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His saying ﴿once more﴾, he said: a second time, the second creation.

Abu Ja'far (al-Tabari) said: The meaning of the speech, then, is: From the earth We brought you out when you were not things, a complete creation, and We will bring you out from it after your deaths a second time, just as We brought you out from it the first time.

* *

The interpretation of His saying: ﴿And We had certainly shown him all Our signs, but he denied and refused﴾ (56):

He, may His remembrance be exalted, says: And We had certainly shown Pharaoh Our signs, meaning Our proofs and arguments for the truth of what We sent with Our two messengers, Musa (Moses) and Harun (Aaron), to him, all of them. ﴿But he denied and refused﴾ to accept from Musa and Harun what they brought from their Lord of the truth, out of arrogance and insolence.

Commentary on the interpretation of His words, exalted is He: ﴿He said, "Have you come to us to drive us out of our land with your magic, O Moses? (57) So we will surely produce for you magic like it. So set between us and you an appointment which neither we nor you will fail to keep, at a place equitable (suwan)."﴾ (58)

His exalted remembrance says: Pharaoh said, when We had shown him all Our signs, to Our messenger Moses: "Have you come to us, O Moses, to drive us out of our homes and dwellings with this magic of yours that you have brought us?" ﴿"So we will surely produce for you magic like it. So set between us and you an appointment"﴾ which we will not exceed, so that we may bring magic like what you have brought, and then we will see which of us overcomes the other. ﴿"Which neither we nor you will fail to keep, at a place equitable (suwan)"﴾ means: at a place of justice and fairness between us and you.

The reciters differed over the reading of this. The majority of the reciters of the Hijaz and Basra and some of the Kufans read ﴿makanan siwan﴾ with a kasra on the sin (sin), while the majority of the reciters of Kufa read ﴿makanan suwan﴾ with a damma on it.

Abu Ja'far (al-Tabari) said: The correct view in this matter, in our opinion, is that both are dialects: the kasra and the damma on the sin of "siwa" are both well known among the Arabs, and scholars among the reciters have read each of them, while their meanings agree. So whichever of them the reciter reads is correct. The Arabs, when it means justice and fairness, have a dialect that is more famous than the kasra and the damma, namely the fatha, as He, great is His praise, said: ﴿"Come to a word equitable (sawa') between us and you"﴾ (Q 3:64). When the sin is fathah it is lengthened (madd); when it is kasrah or dammah it is shortened (qasr), as the poet said:

"Indeed our father had settled in a land, suwan between Qays, Qays of Aylan, and al-Fizr..." [The verse is attributed to Musa ibn Jabir al-Hanafi (Lisan: s-w-y). Al-Akhfash said: siwa when it means "other" or "justice" has three dialects: if the sin is damma or shortened, both are used; if it is fatha, it is lengthened. You say: ma kana siwa, and suwa, and sawa', meaning just and central between the two groups. Musa ibn Jabir said: "We found our father... the verse." Al-Fizr is the father of a clan of Tamim, namely Sa'd ibn Ziyad Manat ibn Tamim.]

Similar to this among nouns are: Tuwa and Tawa, Thunna and Thunna, 'Adan and 'Udan.

Speaking in a manner similar to what we have said, the people of interpretation (ahl al-ta'wil) said:

Bishr related to us, saying: Yazid related to us, saying: Sa'id related to us, from Qatadah: ﴿makanan suwan﴾: that is, just between us and you.

Al-Hasan related to us, saying: 'Abd al-Razzaq informed us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah, regarding His words ﴿makanan suwan﴾: he said: "Equitable between us and you."

Musa related to us, saying: 'Amr related to us, saying: Asbat related to us, from al-Suddi, regarding His words ﴿So set between us and you an appointment which neither we nor you will fail to keep, at a place equitable (suwan)﴾: he said: "He says: just."

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 20, verse 61:

The interpretation of His saying, ﴿Moses said to them, "Woe to you! Do not fabricate a lie against Allah, lest He destroy you with a punishment. Indeed, he fails who fabricates"﴾ (61).

He, exalted is His remembrance, says: Moses said to the magicians when Pharaoh brought them, ﴿"Woe to you! Do not fabricate a lie against Allah"﴾, meaning: do not invent falsehood against Allah, nor attribute words to Him. ﴿"Lest He destroy you with a punishment"﴾, meaning: lest He uproot you with ruin and annihilate you. The Arabs have two forms for this: sahata and asahta; sahata is more common than asahta. From it one says: sahata al-dahr (time destroyed), and asahta mal fulan (he destroyed the wealth of so-and-so), meaning he ruined it; so he yasutuhu suhtan, and asahtahu yusihtuhu ischatan. Among the uses of ischat is the verse of al-Farazdaq:

"The biting of time, O son of Marwan, has left nothing
of the wealth except a remnant ruined or stripped bare."

[[This verse is by al-Farazdaq from his naqida which begins: "You were left with nests, and you scarcely knew how to be left."

Before the verse of testimony he says (see his Diwan, Sawi edition, p. 565): "To you, Commander of the Believers, has driven us
the anxieties of desire and the fearful, arduous journey."

The narration of the verse in the author's text agrees with the narration in (Lisan: jalafa). He said: Abu al-Ghawth said: al-masht: the kingdom. And al-mujallaf: that of which a remnant has been left, or that which has been taken from its sides. Al-mujallaf also: the man whom the years have stripped, meaning they have taken away his wealth. And in it (Lisan: sahata) the saying of the Exalted: (fa-yushtakum bi-adhab): it was read: fa-yashtakum bi-adhab, and yushtakum, with a fatha on the ya and the ha, and yusahhtu (with a damma on the ya) is more common. So fa-sahtakum (with a fatha on the ya and the ha): it peels you. And yusihtakum (with a damma on the ya): it uproots you. And asahta malahu: he uprooted and ruined it. Al-Farazdaq said: "And wiped out the time... or stripped."

As for the raising of mujallaf, it is on the presumption of a subject, as if he said: or he is stripped. The verse is evidence, according to al-Tabari, that the meaning of His saying, fa-yusihtakum, is: uproots you.]]

It is narrated: "wa-massaht aw mujallaf" (with masht).
