Yunus related to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His saying ﴿So He will leave it a level plain﴾: He said: level; al-safsaf: the level.

Yunus related to me, saying: Abdullah ibn Yusuf informed us, saying: Abdullah ibn Lahi'ah related to us, saying: Abu al-Aswad related to us, from Urwah, who said: We were sitting with Abd al-Malik when Ka'b said: The rock is the place of the foot of the Merciful on the Day of Resurrection. He said: Ka'b has lied; the rock is only one of the mountains. Indeed God says, ﴿And they ask you concerning the mountains. Say, "My Lord will blow them away with blowing."﴾ Then Abd al-Malik fell silent.

Muhammad ibn Amr related to me, saying: Abu Asim related to us, saying: Isa related to us; and al-Harith related to me, saying: al-Hasan related to us, saying: Warqa' related to us, all together, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His saying ﴿safsafa﴾: he said: level.

Al-Qasim related to us, saying: al-Husayn related to us, saying: Hajjaj related to me, from Ibn Juraij, from Mujahid, the like of it.

Abu Ja'far said: Some of the scholars of the Arabic language from the people of Kufa used to say: al-qa': the bed where water collects, and al-safsaf: that in which there is no vegetation.

* *

And His saying: ﴿You will not see in it any crookedness or unevenness﴾

That is: you will not see in the earth any crookedness or unevenness.

The people of interpretation differed regarding the meaning of al-awaj and al-amt. Some of them said: by al-awaj in this place is meant the valleys, and by al-amt the hills and elevations.

Those who said so:

Ali related to me, saying: Abu Salih related to us, saying: Mu'awiyah related to me, from Ali, from Ibn Abbas, regarding His saying ﴿You will not see in it crookedness or unevenness﴾: he said: a valley; and al-amt: he said: a hill.

Muhammad ibn Abd Allah al-Makhrami related to me, saying: Abu Amir al-Aqadi related to us, from Abd al-Wahid ibn Safwan, client of Uthman, who said: I heard Ikrimah say: Ibn Abbas was asked about His saying ﴿You will not see in it crookedness or unevenness﴾, and he said: It is the white land, or he said: the smooth land in which there is no raised brick.

Muhammad ibn Amr related to me, saying: Abu Asim related to us, saying: Isa related to us; and al-Harith related to me, saying: al-Hasan related to us, saying: Warqa' related to us, all together, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding ﴿You will not see in it crookedness or unevenness﴾: he said: elevation nor depression.

Yunus related to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His saying ﴿You will not see in it crookedness or unevenness﴾: He said: no enmity; al-amt is al-ta'adi (enmity).

Others said: by al-awaj in this place is meant the cracks, and by al-amt the rise of hills and the like.

Those who said so:

Al-Hasan ibn Yahya related to us, saying: Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Ma'mar informed us, from Qatadah, regarding His saying: ﴿You will not see in it crookedness﴾: he said: a crack; ﴿nor unevenness﴾: he said: nor a mound.

Others said: by al-awaj is meant the slope, and by al-amt the trace.

Those who said so:

Muhammad ibn Sa'd related to me, saying: my father related to me, saying: my uncle related to me, saying: my father related to me, from his father, from Ibn Abbas, regarding His saying ﴿You will not see in it crookedness﴾: he said: you will not see in it a slope; and al-amt: the trace like a sandal strap.

Others said: al-amt: the bends and the humps.

Those who said so:

Bishr related to us, saying: Yazid related to us, saying: Sa'id related to us, from Qatadah, who said: al-amt: the hump.

Abu Ja'far said: The most correct of the sayings concerning this is the saying of the one who said: by al-awaj is meant the slope, because that is what is known in the speech of the Arabs.

If someone says: Is there any crookedness on the earth today, so that it is said: you will not see in it on that day any crookedness? It is said: The meaning of that is: there are no valleys and obstacles in it that prevent the one who looks or travels in it from taking a straight course, as one who takes some of its paths today needs at times to go right and at times left, because of the mountains, valleys and seas in it. As for al-amt, among the Arabs it means bending and weakness, as heard from them: He stretched his rope until he left no amt in it, that is, no bend; and he filled his waterskin until he left no amt in it. From this is the saying of the rajiz (rajaz poet):

"There is no amt in the drawing of his journey"[[The verse is from mashtur rajaz, and it is by al-Ajjaj as in (Lisan al-Arab: amt), and the transmission in it is: * ma fi intiqal rakbihi min amt *

He said: In the hadith of Abu Sa'id al-Khudri: "The Prophet ﷺ prohibited wine, so there is no amt in it, and I forbid intoxication and what intoxicates." Abu Mansur said: The meaning of Abu Sa'id's saying from the Prophet is that he intended that he forbade it with a prohibition in which there is no leniency and no softness, but he made its prohibition severe; and it is from your saying: I travelled a journey with no amt in it, that is, no weakness and no feebleness. It is also possible that the meaning is that he forbade it with a prohibition in which there is no doubt. Its origin is from amt in the sense of estimation and assessment, because doubt enters it. Al-Ajjaj said: * ma fi intiqal rakbihi min amt *

That is, from slackness and limpness. End.]]

That is: from weakness and feebleness. So, if that is the meaning of amt among them, the most correct interpretation of it is: no elevation and no depression, because depression occurs only after elevation. If that is so, the meaning of the speech is: you will not see in it any deviation from evenness, nor elevation, nor depression, but it will be level and smooth, as His saying, the Exalted, states: ﴿a level plain, safsafa﴾.

**The explanation of His words, the Exalted: ﴿On that day they will follow the Caller, with no crookedness in Him, and voices will be hushed before the Most Merciful, so you will hear nothing but a whisper﴾ (20:108)**

He, may His remembrance be exalted, says: On that day people will follow the voice of God's Caller, who calls them to the place of standing on the Day of Resurrection, and He will gather them to Himself. ﴿With no crookedness in Him﴾ means they will not deviate from it or turn away from it. Rather, they will hasten toward it, being driven toward it. It has also been said: "With no crookedness in Him," and the meaning is "with no crookedness in them toward it," because the sense of the statement is what we have mentioned: they will not turn toward Him or away from Him, but will head to Him and come to Him. This is like the expression used in speech: "So-and-so called me to such-and-such, and I have no crookedness regarding it," meaning, "I will not turn away from it."

As for His words ﴿and voices will be hushed before the Most Merciful﴾, He, may His remembrance be exalted, says: the voices of creation will fall silent before the Most Merciful. Thus the voices are described as being humbled, and the meaning, referring to their owners, is that they will all be submissive to their Lord, so that none of them will utter speech except one whom the Most Merciful permits.

As narrated:

Ali told me, saying: Abu Salih told us, saying: Mu'awiyah told me, from Ali, from Ibn Abbas, concerning His words ﴿and voices will be hushed before the Most Merciful﴾, he said: they will be silent.

And as for His words ﴿so you will hear nothing but a whisper﴾:

It is the sound of feet treading toward the place of gathering. Its root meaning is a faint sound. It is said: "So-and-so whispered to so-and-so with his speech" when he confided it to him and concealed it. From this is the verse of the rajaz poet:

*"And they walk with us in a whisper...
If the bird speaks truly, we shall be the ones who prevail."*

[This verse is among those recited by Ibn Abbas. It is transmitted from him by al-Suyuti in al-Itqan and by many exegetes, including the author (al-Tabari). Ibn Manzur in Lisan al-Arab (under h-m-s) quoted its first half: "And they walk with us in a whisper." He said: "It is the sound of the camels' soft feet." Under the entry's opening he said: "Al-hams: the faint sound, the treading, and the eating. In the Revelation: 'so you will hear nothing but a whisper.' In Tahdhib (al-Azhari): he means by it, and God knows best: the rustle of feet on the ground. Al-Farra said: it is said that it is the treading of feet toward the place of gathering, and it is said: a faint sound. It is related from Ibn Abbas that he recited and quoted: 'And they walk with us in a whisper.'"]

By "whisper" he means the sound of camels' feet as they walk.

Those who engage in ta'wil (interpretation of the Qur'an) have said things similar to what we have said on this. 

Mention of those who said so:

Abu Kurayb told us, saying: Ali ibn Abis told us, from Ata, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn Abbas, concerning ﴿so you will hear nothing but a whisper﴾, he said: the treading of feet.

Muhammad ibn Sa'd told me, saying: My father told me, saying: My paternal uncle told me, saying: My father told me, from his father, from Ibn Abbas, concerning His words ﴿and voices will be hushed before the Most Merciful, so you will hear nothing but a whisper﴾, meaning the whisper of feet, which is the treading.

Ali told me, saying: Abdullah told us, saying: Mu'awiyah told me, from Ali, from Ibn Abbas, concerning ﴿so you will hear nothing but a whisper﴾, he said: a faint sound.

Isma'il ibn Musa al-Suddi told us, saying: Shurayk informed us, from Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Asbahani, from Ikrimah, concerning ﴿so you will hear nothing but a whisper﴾, he said: the treading of feet.

Ibn Bashshar told us, saying: Sulayman told us, saying: Hammad told us, from Humayd, from al-Hasan, concerning ﴿so you will hear nothing but a whisper﴾, he said: the whisper of feet.

Bishr told us, saying: Yazid told us, saying: Sa'id told us, from Qatadah, concerning ﴿so you will hear nothing but a whisper﴾. Qatadah said: al-Hasan used to say: the falling of the people's feet.

Yaqub ibn Ibrahim told me, saying: Ibn Ulayyah told us, saying: Ibn Abi Najih told us, from Mujahid, concerning His words ﴿so you will hear nothing but a whisper﴾, he said: "tahafutan" (the sound of soft footfalls), and he said: "takhafut al-kalam" (the speech being lowered).

Muhammad ibn Amr told me, saying: Abu Asim told us, saying: Isa told us; and al-Harith told me, saying: al-Hasan told us, saying: Warqa told us, all from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, concerning His words ﴿hamsan﴾, he said: the lowering of the voice.

Al-Qasim told us, saying: al-Husayn told us, saying: Hajjaj told me, from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujahid, who said: the lowering of the voice. He said: Abdullah ibn Kathir informed me, from Mujahid, who said: a person's speech, whose moving lips and tongue cannot be heard.

Yunus told me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, concerning His words ﴿so you will hear nothing but a whisper﴾: it means you will hear nothing but walking. He said: the whisper is walking, the treading of feet.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 20, verse 109–110:

The interpretation of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿On that Day, intercession will not benefit, except for one whom the Most Merciful has permitted and whose word He has approved. He knows what is before them and what is behind them, but they do not encompass Him in knowledge.﴾

His saying, exalted is His remembrance: ﴿On that Day, intercession will not benefit, except﴾ the intercession of ﴿one whom the Most Merciful has permitted﴾ to intercede, ﴿and whose word He has approved﴾. He added in the speech "lahu" (for him) as evidence for attributing the saying to the pronoun of "man" (whom), and this is like the saying of another speaker: "I approved your deed for you, and I approved it from you." The position of "man" in His saying ﴿except for one whom He has permitted﴾ is in the accusative, because it is an exception from "intercession."

* *

And His saying ﴿He knows what is before them and what is behind them﴾

His saying, exalted is His remembrance: Your Lord, O Muhammad, knows what is before these people who follow the caller, concerning the matter of the Resurrection, and what they will come to in terms of reward and punishment. ﴿And what is behind them﴾: He says, and He knows the matter of what they left behind them of the affairs of the world.

As narrated:

Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding ﴿He knows what is before them﴾: concerning the affair of the Hour, ﴿and what is behind them﴾: concerning the affair of the world.

* *

And His saying ﴿but they do not encompass Him in knowledge﴾

His saying, exalted is His remembrance: His creation does not encompass Him in knowledge. The meaning of the speech is that He encompasses His servants in knowledge, and His servants do not encompass Him in knowledge. Some have claimed that the meaning of this is that God knows what is before His angels and what is behind them, and that His angels do not encompass in knowledge what is before themselves and what is behind them. He said: Those who used to worship the angels are only informed of this, that the angels likewise do not know what is before them and what is behind them, rebuking them and reproaching them with it, that whoever is like this, how could he be worshipped, and that worship is only fitting for one from whom no hidden thing is concealed on earth or in heaven.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 20, verse 109–110:

The interpretation of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿On that Day, intercession will not benefit, except for one whom the Most Merciful has permitted and whose word He has approved. He knows what is before them and what is behind them, but they do not encompass Him in knowledge.﴾

The position of "man" in His saying ﴿except for one whom He has permitted﴾ is in the accusative, because it is an exception from "intercession."

As narrated:

Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding ﴿He knows what is before them﴾: concerning the affair of the Hour, ﴿and what is behind them﴾: concerning the affair of the world.

* *

And His saying ﴿but they do not encompass Him in knowledge﴾

The meaning of the speech is that He encompasses His servants in knowledge, and His servants do not encompass Him in knowledge. He said: Those who used to worship the angels are only informed of this, that the angels likewise do not know what is before them and what is behind them, rebuking them and reproaching them with it, that whoever is like this, how could he be worshipped, and that worship is only fitting for one from whom no hidden thing is concealed on earth or in heaven.

**The commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 20, verse 111:**

**On the interpretation of His words, ﴿And faces shall be humbled before the Ever-Living, the Sustainer of all; and he who bears wrongdoing will have failed﴾**

God, exalted is He, says: The faces of creation shall be humbled and submit to the Ever-Living who does not die, the Sustainer (al-Qayyum) over His creation through His management of them and His disposing of them as He wills. The root of *al-'anw* is humiliation. It is said of it: *'anā wajhahu li-rabbihi ya'nū 'anwan*, meaning he submitted to Him and was humbled. Likewise, a captive is called *'ān* (one in subjection) because of the humiliation of captivity. As for their saying *akhadhtu al-shay' 'anwatan* (I took the thing by force), it may mean that he took it by overpowering it, or that he took it through surrender and obedience, as the poet said:

*Will you obey me, O heart, willingly,*
*when the soul that does not blame itself in its arrogance does not give in?* [[I have not found the name of the poet of this verse. 'Anwatan: In Lisan al-Arab (under '-n-w), in the hadith of the conquest, that he entered Mecca 'anwatan, meaning by force and overpowering. Ibn al-Athir said: it is from 'anā ya'nū, when he is humbled and submissive. The 'anwa is the single instance of it, as if the one taken by it submits and is humiliated. And "the lands were taken 'anwatan," meaning by force and humiliation. Ibn al-A'rabi: 'anā ya'nū means when he took the thing by force. 'Anā ya'nū 'anwatan means when he took the thing by agreement, with honour and gentleness. Al-'anwa also means affection. Al-Azhari said: akhadhtu al-shay' 'anwatan means by overpowering, and it may also mean through surrender and obedience, from what is taken from him. Al-Farra' recited a line by Kuthayyir: "They did not take it 'anwatan out of affection, but the strike of the Mashrafi sword forced it away." So this is in the sense of surrender and obedience without fighting. Al-Akhfash, on God's words "and faces shall be humbled," said: "istaʾsarat" (they became captives). He said: al-'ani is the captive. Abu al-Haytham said: al-'ani is the submissive one.]]

Another poet said:

*Did they not take it 'anwatan out of affection,*
*but by the edge of the Mashrafi sword they forced it away?* [[The line is by Kuthayyir 'Azza, as in (Lisan al-Arab: 'anā), and its meaning was discussed in the previous witness. Al-Mashrafi: a sword attributed to a village called Mashariq in al-Sham or Yemen. Istiqlaluha: taking it and wresting it away.]]

Those who interpret the Qur'an have said what we have said about this.

**Those who said this:**

- Ali narrated to me, saying: Abu Salih told us, saying: Mu'awiya told me, from Ali, from Ibn Abbas, regarding His words "and faces shall be humbled before the Ever-Living, the Sustainer": he said, they were humiliated.

- Muhammad ibn Sa'd narrated to me, saying: my father told me, saying: my paternal uncle told me, saying: my father told me, from his father, from Ibn Abbas, regarding His words "and faces shall be humbled": he meant by *'anat* that they submitted to me.

- Muhammad ibn Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu 'Asim told us, saying: 'Isa told us, and al-Harith told me, saying: al-Hasan told us, saying: Warqa' told us, all of them, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His words "and faces shall be humbled": he said, they became humble.

- Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn told us, saying: Hajjaj told me, from Ibn Juraij, from Mujahid, the same.

- Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid told us, saying: Sa'id told us, from Qatada, regarding His words "and faces shall be humbled before the Ever-Living, the Sustainer": meaning, the faces were humbled before the Ever-Living, the Sustainer.

- Al-Hasan ibn Yahya narrated to us, saying: 'Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Ma'mar informed us, from Qatada, regarding His words "and faces shall be humbled before the Ever-Living, the Sustainer": he said, the faces were humbled.

- Ibn 'Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: al-Mu'tamir ibn Sulayman told us, from his father, saying: Talq said: when a man prostrates, he has humbled his face, or he said: has humbled.

- Abu Husn 'Abd Allah ibn Ahmad narrated to me, saying: 'Abthar told us, saying: Husayn told us, from Amr ibn Murra, from Talq ibn Habib, regarding this verse "and faces shall be humbled before the Ever-Living, the Sustainer": he said, it is the placing of a man's head, his hands, and the tips of his feet (on the ground).

- Abu al-Sa'ib narrated to me, saying: Ibn Fudayl told us, from Layth, from Amr ibn Murra, from Talq ibn Habib, regarding His words: he said, it is your placing your forehead, your palms, your knees, and the tips of your feet in prostration.

- Khallad ibn Aslam narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Fudayl told us, from Husayn, from Amr ibn Murra, from Talq ibn Habib, regarding His words: he said, the placing of the forehead and the nose on the ground.

- Ya'qub narrated to me, saying: Hushaym told us, saying: Husayn informed us, from Amr ibn Murra, from Talq ibn Habib, regarding His words: he said, it is prostration upon the forehead, the palms, the two knees, and the two feet.

- Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His words "and faces shall be humbled before the Ever-Living, the Sustainer": he said, the faces became captives before the Ever-Living, the Sustainer; they all became captives to Him. He said: *al-'ani* is the captive. We have already explained the meaning of "the Ever-Living, the Sustainer" earlier, in a way that makes repeating it here unnecessary.

* * *

**And His words ﴿and he who bears wrongdoing will have failed﴾**

God, exalted is He, says: Whoever carries *zulm* to the place of standing before Him will not attain his need or his aim, by associating partners with God, disbelieving in Him, and acting in disobedience to Him.

Those who interpret the Qur'an have said what we have said about the interpretation of this.

**Those who said this:**

- Al-Hasan ibn Yahya narrated to us, saying: 'Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Ma'mar informed us, from Qatada, regarding His words "and he who bears wrongdoing will have failed": he said, whoever carries *shirk* (associating partners with God).

- Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His words "and he who bears wrongdoing will have failed": he said, whoever carries *shirk*. *Al-zulm* here means *al-shirk*.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 20, verse 112:

The explanation of His words, exalted be He: ﴿And whoever does righteous deeds while he is a believer, he will not fear injustice or diminishment﴾

Says God, may His remembrance be great and His names be sanctified: "And whoever does of righteous deeds," which, it has been said, is the performance of the obligatory duties that God has imposed upon His servants. "While he is a believer" means: while he is affirming God, and that He will requite the people of His obedience and the people of their disobedience for their disobedience. "He will not fear injustice" means: he will not fear from God that He will wrong him, by loading upon him the evil deeds of others and punishing him for them. "Or diminishment" means: he will not fear that his good deeds will be diminished for him, so that their reward is reduced.

And the people of interpretation (ahl al-ta'wil) have said in accordance with what we have said regarding this.

Mention of those who said this:

Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding His words ﴿And whoever does righteous deeds while he is a believer﴾: "Indeed, God accepts from deeds only that which is in faith."

Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: he said: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Juraij, regarding His words ﴿And whoever does righteous deeds while he is a believer﴾, he said: "They claim that they are the obligatory duties."

Mention of those who said what we have said regarding the meaning of His words ﴿He will not fear injustice or diminishment﴾:

Abu Kurayb and Sulayman ibn Abd al-Jabbar narrated to us, both saying: Ibn Atiyyah narrated to us, from Isra'il, from Simak, from Ikrimah, from Ibn Abbas, regarding ﴿He will not fear injustice or diminishment﴾, he said: "Hadman (diminishment): usurpation."

Ali narrated to me, saying: Abu Salih narrated to us, saying: Mu'awiyah narrated to me, from Ali, from Ibn Abbas, who said regarding ﴿He will not fear injustice or diminishment﴾: "The son of Adam will not fear on the Day of Resurrection that he will be wronged by having his evil deeds increased, nor that he will be wronged by having his good deeds diminished."

Muhammad ibn Sa'd narrated to me, saying: my father narrated to me, saying: my paternal uncle narrated to me, saying: my father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn Abbas, regarding His words ﴿And whoever does righteous deeds while he is a believer, he will not fear injustice or diminishment﴾, he said: "He says: I am the Subduer over you today; I will seize you by My power and My severity, and I am capable of subduing you and diminishing you. Rather, between Me and you is justice, and that is the Day of Resurrection."

It was reported to me from al-Husayn ibn al-Faraj, who said: I heard Abu Mu'adh say: Ubayd ibn Sulayman informed us, saying: I heard al-Dahhak say regarding His words ﴿He will not fear injustice or diminishment﴾: "As for hadman, it is that a man does not overpower another man by his strength. God says on the Day of Resurrection: 'I will not seize you by My power and My severity; rather, justice is between Me and you, and there will be no injustice upon you.'"

Muhammad ibn Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu Asim narrated to us, saying: Isa narrated to us, and al-Harith narrated to me, saying: al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Warqa' narrated to us, all of them, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His words ﴿hadman﴾, he said: "The reduction of something from the due of his deed."

Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Juraij, from Mujahid, the like of it.

Musa ibn Abd al-Rahman al-Masruqi narrated to me, saying: Abu Usamah narrated to us, from Mis'ar, who said: I heard Habib ibn Abi Thabit say regarding His words ﴿or diminishment﴾: "Hadm: reduction."

Al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Ma'mar informed us, from Qatadah, regarding His words ﴿He will not fear injustice or diminishment﴾, he said: "Injustice would be that evil deeds be increased for him, and diminishment that good deeds be reduced for him."

Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding His words ﴿He will not fear injustice or diminishment﴾, he said: "He does not fear being wronged so as not to be recompensed for his deed, nor fear that his due be diminished so that his deed is not paid in full."

Al-Harith narrated to us, saying: al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Salam ibn Miskin narrated to us, from Maymun ibn Siyah, from al-Hasan, regarding the words of God Almighty ﴿He will not fear injustice or diminishment﴾, he said: "God does not reduce anything from his good deeds, and the sin of the wrongdoer is not laid upon him."

The root of hadm is reduction. It is said: "So-and-so diminished my right for me (hadamani haqqi)," and from it comes "a woman who is hadim," meaning one with a flat (slender) belly. And from it the saying: "The food has been digested (hadama al-ta'am)" when it has gone away. And "I have diminished (hadamtu) a part of your right for you," meaning I have reduced it for you.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 20, verse 113:

The interpretation of His saying, the Exalted: ﴿And thus We have sent it down as an Arabic Qur'an, and We have diversified therein some of the warnings, that they may fear Allah, or it may cause them to take heed.﴾

His saying, may His remembrance be exalted, means: Just as We encouraged the people of faith toward righteous deeds by promising them what We promised them, so too We warned the people of disbelief, through threats, against persisting in Our disobedience and in their disbelief in Our signs. Thus We sent down this Qur'an in Arabic, since they were Arabs. ﴿And We have diversified therein some of the warnings﴾: that is, We have explained therein, meaning: We have frightened them in it with various kinds of threat. ﴿That they may fear Us﴾: that is, that they may guard themselves against Us, by Our varying in it the threats We have varied. ﴿Or it may cause them to take heed﴾: that is, or this Qur'an may produce in them a reminder, so that they may take lesson and be admonished by what We did to the nations that denied the messengers before them, and so that they may desist from the disbelief in Allah in which they persist.

Ahl al-ta'wil (the scholars of exegesis) have said things similar to what we have said about this.

Mention of those who said so:

Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding ﴿And thus We have sent it down as an Arabic Qur'an, and We have diversified therein some of the warnings, that they may fear Allah﴾: what they were warned about regarding the command of Allah and His punishment, and His dealings with the nations before them. ﴿Or it may cause them to take heed﴾: the Qur'an. ﴿A reminder﴾: that is, diligence and piety (wara').

Al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: 'Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Ma'mar informed us, from Qatadah, concerning His saying ﴿Or it may cause them to take heed, a reminder﴾, he said: diligence and piety. Some of them have also said concerning ﴿Or it may cause them to take heed, a reminder﴾ that its meaning is: or it may cause for them honour (sharaf) through their faith in it.

The commentary on the verse: "So exalted is Allah, the King, the Truth. And do not hasten with the Qur'an before its revelation is completed to you, and say: My Lord, increase me in knowledge" (20:114).

Al-Tabari said: Allah, may His remembrance be exalted, says: Exalted is He to whom worship is due from all His creation, the King whose authority overcomes every king and tyrant, the Truth above what the polytheists among His creation attribute to Him. "And do not hasten with the Qur'an before its revelation is completed to you." Allah, may His praise be exalted, says to His Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ): Do not hasten, O Muhammad, with the Qur'an, by reciting it to your companions or reading it to them, before its meanings are made clear to you by revelation. He was rebuked for dictating and having dictated to others what Allah had sent down to him of His Book before he had been shown its meanings. It was also said: Do not recite it to anyone, nor dictate it to anyone, until We have explained it to you.

The people of interpretation have said things similar to what we have said on this matter.

Those who said that:

Muhammad ibn 'Amr related to me, saying: Abu 'Asim told us, saying: 'Isa told us; and al-Harith related to me, saying: al-Hasan told us, saying: Warqa' told us, all of them from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His words "And do not hasten with the Qur'an before its revelation is completed to you": he said: Do not recite it to anyone until We have explained it to you.

al-Qasim told us, saying: al-Husayn told us, saying: Hajjaj related to me, from Ibn Jurayj, who said: He says: Do not recite it to anyone until We complete it for you. Thus al-Qasim said: "until We complete it" (natimmahu).

Muhammad ibn Sa'd related to me, saying: my father related to me, saying: my paternal uncle related to me, saying: my father related to me, from his father, from Ibn 'Abbas.

* *

His words "And do not hasten with the Qur'an before its revelation is completed to you."

Meaning: Do not hasten until We explain it to you.

Bishr told us, saying: Yazid told us, saying: Sa'id told us, from Qatadah, regarding "And do not hasten with the Qur'an before its revelation is completed to you": i.e., its explanation (bayanahu).

al-Hasan told us, saying: 'Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Ma'mar informed us, from Qatadah, regarding "And do not hasten with the Qur'an before its revelation is completed to you": he said: its clarification (tibyanahu).

Ibn al-Muthanna and Ibn Bashshar told us, both saying: Muhammad ibn Ja'far told us, saying: Shu'bah told us, from Qatadah, regarding "before its revelation is completed to you": before its explanation is made clear to you.

* *

His words "And say: My Lord, increase me in knowledge."

Allah, may His remembrance be exalted, says: And say, O Muhammad: My Lord, increase me in knowledge, in addition to what You have taught me, by asking Him for benefits of knowledge that I do not know.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 20, verse 115:

The interpretation of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And We had already made a covenant with Adam before, but he forgot; and We found in him no determination﴾

He, exalted is His remembrance, says: "And if these people to whom We have diversified the threat in this Qur'an, O Muhammad, neglect My covenant, oppose My command, abandon My obedience, and follow the command of their enemy Iblis, obeying him in opposition to My command, then how often has their father Adam done the same. ﴿And We had already made a covenant with﴾, meaning: We had already charged Adam and said to him, ﴿Indeed, this is an enemy to you and to your wife, so let him not get you both out of Paradise﴾, but Satan whispered to him and he obeyed him and opposed My command, so there befell him of My punishment what befell him."

And by His saying, may His praise be glorified, ﴿before﴾, He means these people about whom He informed that He has diversified the threat for them in this Qur'an. As for His saying ﴿but he forgot﴾, it means: he abandoned My covenant.

As related:

* Ali related to me, he said: Abu Salih related to us, he said: Mu'awiyah related to me, from Ali, from Ibn Abbas, regarding His saying ﴿And We had already made a covenant with Adam before, but he forgot﴾, he said: "He abandoned."

* Al-Hasan related to us, he said: Abd al-Razzaq informed us, he said: Ma'mar informed us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His saying ﴿but he forgot﴾, he said: "He abandoned the command of his Lord."

* Yunus related to me, he said: Ibn Wahb informed us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His saying ﴿And We had already made a covenant with Adam before, but he forgot; and We found in him no determination﴾, he said: He said to him, ﴿O Adam, indeed this is an enemy to you and to your wife, so let him not get you both out of Paradise, and [you] will be distressed﴾, and he recited until he reached ﴿Indeed, you will not be hungry therein or be unclothed﴾, and he recited until he reached ﴿and a kingdom that will not deteriorate﴾. He said: "So he forgot what he had been charged with in that. He said: This was the covenant of God to him. He said: Had he possessed determination, he would not have obeyed his enemy who envied him, and he would have refused to prostrate to Him alongside those who prostrated, whom Iblis refused to join, and he would not have disobeyed God who honoured him and ennobled him, and commanded His angels, and they prostrated to him."

* Ibn al-Muthanna and Ibn Bashshar related to us, they both said: Yahya ibn Sa'id, Abd al-Rahman and Mu'ammil related to us, they said: Sufyan related to us, from al-A'mash, from Muslim al-Batin, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn Abbas, who said: "Man was only named insan (human) because he was given a covenant and forgot it."

* * *

As for His saying ﴿and We found in him no determination﴾

The people of interpretation differed regarding the meaning of ʿazm (determination) here. Some of them said: its meaning is patience.

Those who said that:

* Bishr related to us, he said: Yazid related to us, he said: Sa'id related to us, from Qatadah, regarding His saying ﴿and We found in him no determination﴾, meaning: patience.

* Muhammad ibn Bashshar related to us, he said: Muhammad ibn Ja'far related to us, he said: Shu'bah related to us, from Qatadah, ﴿and We found in him no determination﴾, he said: patience.

* Ibrahim ibn Ya'qub al-Jawzajani related to us, he said: Abu al-Nadr related to us, he said: Shu'bah related to us, from Qatadah, the like of it.

Others said: rather, its meaning is: retention (hifz), and they said: its meaning is: We did not find in him retention of what We had covenanted with him.

Those who said that:

* Abu al-Sa'ib related to me, he said: Ibn Idris related to us, from his father, from Atiyyah, regarding ﴿and We found in him no determination﴾, he said: retention of what I commanded him.

* Ya'qub ibn Ibrahim related to me, he said: Hashim ibn al-Qasim related to us, from al-Ash'ajī, from Sufyan, from Amr ibn Qays, from Atiyyah, regarding His saying ﴿and We found in him no determination﴾, he said: retention.

* Abbad ibn Muhammad related to us, he said: Qabisah related to us, from Sufyan, from Amr ibn Qays, from Atiyyah, regarding His saying ﴿and We found in him no determination﴾, he said: retention of what I commanded him with.

* Muhammad ibn Sa'd related to me, he said: my father related to me, he said: my paternal uncle related to me, he said: my father related to me, from his father, from Ibn Abbas, His saying ﴿and We found in him no determination﴾, he says: We did not find in him retention.

* Yunus related to me, he said: Ibn Wahb informed us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His saying ﴿and We found in him no determination﴾, he said: ʿazm is: keeping to what Allah, blessed and exalted, commanded him to preserve, and holding fast to it.

* Ali related to me, he said: Abu Salih related to us, he said: Mu'awiyah related to me, from Ali, from Ibn Abbas, regarding His saying ﴿and We found in him no determination﴾, he says: We did not make for him determination.

* Al-Qasim related to me, he said: Al-Husayn related to us, he said: al-Hajjaj ibn Fudalah related to us, from Luqman ibn Amir, from Abu Umamah, who said: "If the forbearance of the children of Adam were gathered from the day Allah, exalted is He, created Adam until the Hour, and placed in one pan of a scale, and the forbearance of Adam were placed in the other pan, his forbearance would outweigh their forbearance. And Allah, exalted is He, has said: ﴿and We found in him no determination﴾."

Abu Ja'far (al-Tabari) said: The root of ʿazm is the heart's firm resolve upon a thing; it is said of someone: "ʿazama fulan ʿala kadhā" (so-and-so resolved upon such-and-such) when he resolves upon it and intends it. From the firm resolve of the heart is the retention of a thing, and from it is patience upon a thing, because no one who is distressed becomes distressed except from the weakness and frailty of his heart. Given that this is so, there is no meaning more eloquent than what Allah, blessed and exalted, has explained in His saying ﴿and We found in him no determination﴾. Its interpretation is: We did not find in him determination of heart, in fulfilling his covenant with Allah, nor in retaining what he was charged with.

The interpretation of His saying: ﴿And when We said to the angels, "Prostrate yourselves before Adam," they prostrated, except Iblis; he refused﴾ [20:116] ﴿Then We said, "O Adam, indeed this is an enemy to you and to your wife, so let him not drive you both out of the Garden, lest you be made wretched"﴾ [20:117].

He, exalted is His remembrance, says, instructing His Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ) about what occurred regarding Adam's neglect of his covenant, and informing him that his offspring would not deviate from Adam's course in this, except for those whom Allah protects among them. ﴿And﴾ mention, O Muhammad, ﴿when We said to the angels, "Prostrate yourselves before Adam," they prostrated, except Iblis; he refused﴾ to prostrate to him. ﴿Then We said, "O Adam, indeed this is an enemy to you and to your wife"﴾ and because of his enmity toward you he did not prostrate to you, and he opposed My command in that and disobeyed Me. ﴿So do not obey him in what he orders you, lest he drive you both out of the Garden by your disobedience to your Lord and your obedience to him﴾ ﴿"...lest you be made wretched"﴾ means: your living will then be from the toil of your hand, and that is his wretchedness against which his Lord warned him.

As related:

⁕ Ibn Humayd narrated to us, he said: Ya'qub narrated to us, from Ja'far, from Sa'id, who said: A red bull was sent down to Adam, and he would plough with it and wipe the sweat from his brow. This is what Allah, exalted is His remembrance, meant by His saying: ﴿So let him not drive you both out of the Garden, lest you be made wretched﴾, and that was his wretchedness. Allah, exalted is His remembrance, said ﴿lest you be made wretched﴾ and did not say "lest you both be made wretched," though He had said ﴿let him not drive you both out﴾, because the beginning of the address from Allah was to Adam, peace be upon him. So in informing him of the punishment for his disobedience in what He had forbidden him, from eating of the tree, there was sufficiency in mentioning the woman, since it was known that her ruling in this was the same as his. Like His saying ﴿one sitting on the right and one on the left﴾, where the meaning is understood by the hearers from mention of the action of its companion.

The commentary on the words of Allah, the Exalted, "Indeed, for you there is [the promise] that you will not hunger therein, nor go naked, And that you will not thirst therein, nor be exposed to the sun" (20:118–119), and "Then Satan whispered to him, saying, 'O Adam, shall I direct you to the tree of eternity and a kingdom that does not decay?'" (20:120).

He, may His remembrance be exalted, says, relating His saying to Adam when He settled him in the Garden: "Indeed, for you [O Adam]" "there is that you will not hunger therein, nor go naked." The "an" (that) in His saying "that you will not hunger therein, nor go naked" is in a position of accusative governed by the "inna" (indeed) in His saying "Indeed, for you."

* *

As for His saying "And that you will not thirst therein,"

The reciters differed in its recitation. Some reciters of Madina and Kufa read it with a kasra: "wa-inna-ka" (and indeed you), taking it as a conjunction upon His saying "Indeed, for you." Some reciters of Madina, and the majority of the reciters of Kufa and Basra, read it with a fatha on its alif: "wa-anna-ka" (and that you), conjoining it to the "an" in His saying "that you will not hunger therein, nor go naked." They directed the interpretation to mean that for you is this and that. This reading is the more preferred of the two readings in my view, because Allah, blessed and exalted is His remembrance, promised this to Adam when He settled him in the Garden. So making it a conjunction upon "an la tajू' (that you will not hunger)" is more preferable than making it the predicate of a new subject, although the latter is not far from correct. By His saying "that you will not thirst therein," He means: you will not be thirsty in the Garden as long as you are in it. "Nor be exposed to the sun" means: you will not come out into the sun so that its heat harms you, as Ibn Abi Rabi'ah said:

*She saw a man who, when the sun confronted him, exposed himself to it, and when evening came, was chilled.*

[[The verse is by Umar ibn Abi Rabi'ah al-Qurashi al-Makhzumi. Ibn Manzur cited it in Lisan al-Arab under (ḍaḥā) without attributing it. He said: "Daha al-rajul dahwan (on the pattern fa'ala) and duhwan (on the pattern fu'ul) and duhiya: he came out into the sun; and daha (with kasra on the ha') yadha in both dialects, with the verbal noun duhwan and duhiya: the sun struck him." He said: Allah the Exalted said: "And that you will not thirst therein nor be exposed to the sun," and said: it means the heat of the sun will not harm you. Al-Farra' said: "la tadha" means no harmful sun will strike you. He said: In some tafsir: "wa-la tadha" means you will not sweat. Al-Azhari said: The first is closer to the correct meaning, and he recited: "She saw a man..." The word "yakhsar" is from khasar (with a vowel on the kha'), the cold a person feels in his extremities.]]

This is in accordance with what we have said, and the people of interpretation said the same.

Those who said that:

* Ali related to me, saying: Abu Salih related to us, saying: Mu'awiya related to me, from Ali, from Ibn Abbas, regarding His saying "And that you will not thirst therein nor be exposed to the sun": he said: no thirst or heat will afflict you therein.

* Muhammad ibn Sa'd related to me, saying: my father related to me, saying: my uncle related to me, saying: my father related to me, from his father, from Ibn Abbas, regarding His saying "And that you will not thirst therein nor be exposed to the sun": he said: no heat or harm will afflict you.

* Ahmad ibn Uthman ibn Hakim al-Awdi related to me, saying: Abd al-Rahman ibn Shurayk related to us, saying: my father related to me, from Khusayf, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, "You will not thirst therein nor be exposed to the sun": he said: the sun will not reach you.

* Bishr related to us, saying: Yazid related to us, saying: Sa'id related to us, from Qatada, "nor be exposed to the sun": he said: the sun will not reach you. As for His saying "Then Satan whispered to him," He means: Satan cast into Adam's mind and spoke to him. "He said, 'O Adam, shall I direct you to the tree of eternity'" means: he said to him: shall I direct you to a tree which, if you eat from it, you will live forever and not die, and you will possess a kingdom that does not end or decay.

As follows:

* Musa related to me, saying: Amr related to us, saying: Asbat related to us, from al-Suddi, regarding "O Adam, shall I direct you to the tree of eternity and a kingdom that does not decay?": If you eat from it, you will become a king like God, "or you will be among the immortals," so that you both will never die.
