He said: "Daha al-rajul dahwan (on the pattern fa'ala) and duhwan (on the pattern fu'ul) and duhiya: he came out into the sun; and daha (with kasra on the ha') yadha in both dialects, with the verbal noun duhwan and duhiya: the sun struck him." He said: Allah the Exalted said: "And that you will not thirst therein nor be exposed to the sun," and said: it means the heat of the sun will not harm you. Al-Farra' said: "la tadha" means no harmful sun will strike you. He said: In some tafsir: "wa-la tadha" means you will not sweat. Al-Azhari said: The first is closer to the correct meaning, and he recited: "She saw a man..." The word "yakhsar" is from khasar (with a vowel on the kha'), the cold a person feels in his extremities.]]

This is in accordance with what we have said, and the people of interpretation said the same.

Those who said that:

* Ali related to me, saying: Abu Salih related to us, saying: Mu'awiya related to me, from Ali, from Ibn Abbas, regarding His saying "And that you will not thirst therein nor be exposed to the sun": he said: no thirst or heat will afflict you therein.

* Muhammad ibn Sa'd related to me, saying: my father related to me, saying: my uncle related to me, saying: my father related to me, from his father, from Ibn Abbas, regarding His saying "And that you will not thirst therein nor be exposed to the sun": he said: no heat or harm will afflict you.

* Ahmad ibn Uthman ibn Hakim al-Awdi related to me, saying: Abd al-Rahman ibn Shurayk related to us, saying: my father related to me, from Khusayf, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, "You will not thirst therein nor be exposed to the sun": he said: the sun will not reach you.

* Bishr related to us, saying: Yazid related to us, saying: Sa'id related to us, from Qatada, "nor be exposed to the sun": he said: the sun will not reach you. As for His saying "Then Satan whispered to him," He means: Satan cast into Adam's mind and spoke to him. "He said, 'O Adam, shall I direct you to the tree of eternity'" means: he said to him: shall I direct you to a tree which, if you eat from it, you will live forever and not die, and you will possess a kingdom that does not end or decay.

As follows:

* Musa related to me, saying: Amr related to us, saying: Asbat related to us, from al-Suddi, regarding "O Adam, shall I direct you to the tree of eternity and a kingdom that does not decay?": If you eat from it, you will become a king like God, "or you will be among the immortals," so that you both will never die.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 20, verse 121–122:

The interpretation of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Then they both ate from it, and their private parts became apparent to them, and they began to fasten over themselves some leaves of the Garden. And Adam disobeyed his Lord, and so he erred﴾ [20:121].

He, exalted is His remembrance, says: Adam and Hawwa' ate from the tree which they had been forbidden to eat from, and obeyed the command of Iblis, and disobeyed the command of their Lord. ﴿Their private parts became apparent to them﴾ means: their private parts were uncovered for them, and they had been concealed from their eyes.

As related by:

* Musa related to me, he said: Amr related to us, he said: Asbat related to us, from al-Suddi, he said: Iblis only intended, by his saying ﴿Shall I direct you to the tree of eternity and a kingdom that does not decay?﴾ [20:120], to make apparent to them what had been hidden from them of their private parts, by stripping them of their clothing. He had known that they had private parts because he had read from the books of the angels, but Adam did not know that. Their clothing had been nails (of light). Adam refused to eat from it, so Hawwa' went ahead and ate, then she said: "O Adam, eat, for I have eaten and it has not harmed me." So when Adam ate, their private parts became apparent.

* *

And His saying ﴿and they began to fasten over themselves some leaves of the Garden﴾

means: they began to tie over themselves some leaves of the Garden.

As related by:

* Musa related to us, he said: Amr related to us, he said: Asbat related to us, from al-Suddi: ﴿and they began to fasten over themselves some leaves of the Garden﴾ means: they began to cover themselves with fig leaves.

* Bishr related to us, he said: Yazid related to us, he said: Sa'id related to us, from Qatadah, regarding His saying ﴿and they began to fasten over themselves some leaves of the Garden﴾: it means they began to join together over themselves some leaves of the Garden.

* *

And His saying ﴿And Adam disobeyed his Lord, and so he erred﴾

means: he disobeyed the command of his Lord, and transgressed to what was not permitted for him to transgress to, namely eating from the tree from which He had forbidden him to eat. And His saying ﴿Then his Lord chose him, and turned to him in forgiveness, and guided him﴾ means: his Lord chose him after his disobedience to Him, granted him to return to what pleases Him, and to act in obedience to Him; and that is the repentance which He accepted from him. And His saying ﴿and guided him﴾ means: He guided him to repentance, and enabled him to it.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 20, verse 121–122:

The interpretation of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Then they both ate from it, and their private parts became apparent to them, and they began to fasten over themselves some leaves of the Garden. And Adam disobeyed his Lord, and so he erred﴾ [20:121].

He, exalted is His remembrance, says: Adam and Hawwa' ate from the tree which they had been forbidden to eat from, and obeyed the command of Iblis, and disobeyed the command of their Lord. ﴿Their private parts became apparent to them﴾ means: their private parts were uncovered for them, and they had been concealed from their eyes.

As related by:

* Musa related to me, he said: Amr related to us, he said: Asbat related to us, from al-Suddi, he said: Iblis only intended, by his saying ﴿Shall I direct you to the tree of eternity and a kingdom that does not decay?﴾ [20:120], to make apparent to them what had been hidden from them of their private parts, by stripping them of their clothing. He had known that they had private parts because he had read from the books of the angels, but Adam did not know that. Their clothing had been nails (of light). Adam refused to eat from it, so Hawwa' went ahead and ate, then she said: "O Adam, eat, for I have eaten and it has not harmed me." So when Adam ate, their private parts became apparent.

* *

And His saying ﴿and they began to fasten over themselves some leaves of the Garden﴾

means: they began to tie over themselves some leaves of the Garden.

As related by:

* Musa related to us, he said: Amr related to us, he said: Asbat related to us, from al-Suddi: ﴿and they began to fasten over themselves some leaves of the Garden﴾ means: they began to cover themselves with fig leaves.

* Bishr related to us, he said: Yazid related to us, he said: Sa'id related to us, from Qatadah, regarding His saying ﴿and they began to fasten over themselves some leaves of the Garden﴾: it means they began to join together over themselves some leaves of the Garden.

* *

And His saying ﴿And Adam disobeyed his Lord, and so he erred﴾

means: he disobeyed the command of his Lord, and transgressed to what was not permitted for him to transgress to, namely eating from the tree from which He had forbidden him to eat. And His saying ﴿Then his Lord chose him, and turned to him in forgiveness, and guided him﴾ means: his Lord chose him after his disobedience to Him, granted him to return to what pleases Him, and to act in obedience to Him; and that is the repentance which He accepted from him. And His saying ﴿and guided him﴾ means: He guided him to repentance, and enabled him to it.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 20, verse 123:

The interpretation of His saying, the Exalted: ﴿He said: "Go down from it, all of you, some of you enemies to others. And if guidance comes to you from Me, then whoever follows My guidance will neither go astray nor be distressed."﴾

His saying, may He be remembered, means: God the Exalted said to Adam and Eve, ﴿Go down from it, all of you, to the earth, some of you enemies to others.﴾ That is: you two are the enemy of Iblis and his offspring, and Iblis is the enemy of you two and your offspring.

* *

And His saying ﴿And if guidance comes to you from Me﴾

That is: if guidance comes to you, O Adam and Eve, and to Iblis, from Me, meaning a clarification of My way and of the religion I choose for My creatures. ﴿Then whoever follows My guidance﴾ means: whoever follows that clarification of Mine and acts upon it, and does not deviate from it, ﴿will neither go astray﴾ means: he will not depart from the path of truth, but he will be guided in this world and will be rightly guided, ﴿nor be distressed﴾ in the Hereafter through the punishment of God, because God will admit him into the Garden and deliver him from His punishment.

Those versed in interpretation have said things similar to what we have said regarding the interpretation of this.

Mention of those who said that:

* Al-Husayn ibn Yazid al-Tahhan narrated to me, saying: Abu Khalid al-Ahmar narrated to us, from Amr ibn Qays al-Mula'i, from Ikrimah, from Ibn Abbas, who said: God guaranteed for whoever recites the Qur'an and follows what is in it that he will not go astray in this world nor be distressed in the Hereafter. Then he recited this verse: ﴿Then whoever follows My guidance will neither go astray nor be distressed.﴾

* Nasr ibn Abd al-Rahman al-Awdi narrated to me, saying: Hakkam al-Razi narrated to us, from Ayyub ibn Musa, from Marw, from al-Mula'i, from Ibn Abbas, that he said: Indeed God has guaranteed.... and he mentioned something similar.

* Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Hakkam narrated to us, from Ayyub ibn Yasar Abu Abd al-Rahman, from Amr ibn Qays, from a man, from Ibn Abbas, with something similar.

* Ali ibn Sahl al-Ramli narrated to us, saying: Ahmad ibn Muhammad al-Nasai narrated to us, from Abu Salamah, from Ata, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, who said: Ibn Abbas said: Whoever recites the Qur'an and follows what is in it, God will protect him from misguidance and shield him, I think he said: from the terror of the Day of Resurrection, because He said: ﴿Then whoever follows My guidance will neither go astray nor be distressed﴾ in the Hereafter.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 20, verses 124–126:

The interpretation of His, may He be exalted, saying: ﴿And whoever turns away from My remembrance, indeed he will have a narrow life, and We will gather him on the Day of Resurrection blind. He will say, "My Lord, why have You gathered me blind, while I had been seeing?" He will say, "Thus Our signs came to you, but you forgot them; and thus today you are forgotten."﴾

His, may He be exalted and remembered, says: ﴿And whoever turns away from My remembrance﴾, meaning the reminder with which I remind him, so he turns away from it, does not accept it, does not respond to it, and is not admonished by it, so that he refrains from what he persists in of disobedience to his Lord's command. ﴿Indeed, he will have a narrow life﴾ means: indeed, he will have a constricted life. The word ḍank (narrow, straitened) applied to dwellings, places and livelihoods means severe: one says, "This is a ḍank dwelling" when it is cramped, and "ʿaysh ḍank" (a straitened life). The masculine and feminine, the singular and dual and plural, are used with one form. From it is the saying of ʿAntarah:

"And if they alight in a ḍank place, I alight (with them)."
[[This is part of the second half of a verse by ʿAntarah ibn ʿAmr ibn Shaddad al-ʿAbsi (Mukhtar al-Shiʿr al-Jahili, al-Halabi edition, sharh Mustafa al-Saqqa, p. 388). The full verse is: "If they are overtaken, I charge; if they are pressed in battle, I hold firm; and if they are found in a ḍank place, I alight."]]

And in Lisan (entry ḍ-n-k): ḍank means narrowness of anything; the masculine and feminine are alike in it. A ḍank livelihood is a constricted one. In the Revelation: "Indeed, he will have a narrow life," i.e., not lawful.

Those who interpret the Qur'an said what we have said in this regard.

Those who said that:

- Ali narrated to me, saying: ʿAbd Allah narrated to us, saying: Muʿawiyah narrated to me, from ʿAli, from Ibn ʿAbbas, regarding His saying ﴿indeed, he will have a narrow life﴾: he says: wretchedness.

- Muhammad ibn ʿAmr narrated to me, saying: Abu ʿAsim narrated to us, saying: ʿIsa narrated to us, and al-Harith narrated to me, saying: al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Warqa' narrated to us, all from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His saying ﴿ḍankan﴾: he said: constricted.

- al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: ʿAbd al-Razzaq narrated to us, from Maʿmar, from Qatadah, regarding His saying ﴿indeed, he will have a narrow life﴾: he said: The ḍank is the narrowness.

- Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Hakkam narrated to us, from ʿAnbasah, from Muhammad ibn ʿAbd al-Rahman, from al-Qasim ibn Abi Bazzah, from Mujahid, regarding His saying ﴿indeed, he will have a narrow life﴾: he says: constricted.

- al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujahid, the like of it.

The interpreters differed regarding the place where Allah placed for those who turn away from His remembrance the narrow life, and the state in which He placed them. Some of them said: He placed it for them in the Hereafter, in Hell, because their food there is ḍarīʿ and zaqqum.

Those who said that:

- Muhammad ibn ʿAmr ibn ʿAli ibn Muqaddam narrated to me, saying: Yahya ibn Saʿid narrated to us, from ʿAwf, from al-Hasan, regarding His saying: ﴿indeed, he will have a narrow life﴾: he said: in Hell.

- Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His saying ﴿And whoever turns away from My remembrance, indeed he will have a narrow life﴾, then he recited until he reached ﴿and does not believe in the signs of his Lord﴾, and said: These are the people of disbelief. He said: As for a narrow life, in the Fire there are thorns of fire, zaqqum and ghislin, and the ḍarīʿ is a thorn of fire. There is no livelihood in the grave or in this world; livelihood and life are only in the Hereafter. He recited the saying of Allah, mighty and majestic: ﴿Would that I had sent ahead for my life﴾ and said: "for my livelihood." He said: The ghislin and zaqqum are things that the people of this world do not know.

- al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: ʿAbd al-Razzaq narrated to us, from Maʿmar, from Qatadah: ﴿indeed, he will have a narrow life﴾: he said: in the Fire.

Others said: Rather, He meant by it: indeed, he will have a livelihood in this world that is unlawful. He said: Allah, mighty and majestic, described their livelihood as narrow, because unlawful wealth, even if it is abundant, is narrow.

Those who said that:

- Muhammad ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Yahya ibn Wadih narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn ibn Waqid narrated to us, from Yazid, from ʿIkrimah, regarding His saying: ﴿a narrow livelihood﴾: he said: It is the livelihood in which Allah gave him abundance from the unlawful.

- Dawud ibn Sulayman ibn Yazid al-Mukatib, from the people of Basra, narrated to me, saying: ʿAmr ibn Jarir al-Bajali narrated to us, from Isma'il ibn Abi Khalid, from Qays ibn Abi Hazim, regarding the saying of Allah ﴿a narrow livelihood﴾: he said: a provision in disobedience to Him.

- ʿAbd al-ʿAla ibn Wasil narrated to me, saying: Yaʿla ibn ʿUbayd narrated to us, saying: Abu Bistam narrated to us, from al-Dahhak, ﴿indeed, he will have a narrow life﴾: he said: the evil earning.

- Muhammad ibn Isma'il al-Sarrari narrated to me, saying: Muhammad ibn Sawwar narrated to us, saying: Abu al-Yaqzan ʿAmmar ibn Muhammad narrated to us, from Harun ibn Muhammad al-Taymi, from al-Dahhak, regarding His saying ﴿indeed, he will have a narrow life﴾: he said: the evil deed and the bad provision.

Others, among those who said that He meant that these people have a narrow life in this world, said: It is only called narrow although it is wide, because they spend what they spend of their wealth while disbelieving in Allah's replacement and despairing of Allah's bounty, and having an evil opinion of their Lord; so their livelihood becomes harsh and constricted for them because of that.

Those who said that:

- Muhammad ibn Saʿd narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, saying: My paternal uncle narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn ʿAbbas, regarding His saying ﴿And whoever turns away from My remembrance, indeed he will have a narrow life﴾: he says: Every wealth I give to a servant of Mine, whether little or much, in which he does not fear Me, has no good in it, and it is the narrowness in livelihood. It is said that some astray people turned away from the truth, and they were people of abundance and wealth in this world, but their livelihood was narrow. That is because they used to think that Allah, mighty and majestic, would not replace their livelihoods, out of their evil opinion of Allah and their denial of Him. When a servant denies Allah and has an evil opinion of Him, his livelihood becomes harsh upon him, and that is the ḍank.

Others said: Rather, He meant by it: that this is for them in the barzakh, which is the punishment of the grave.

Those who said that:

- Yazid ibn Makhlad al-Wasiti narrated to me, saying: Khalid ibn ʿAbd Allah narrated to us, from ʿAbd al-Rahman ibn Ishaq, from Abu Hazim, from al-Nuʿman ibn Abi ʿAyyash, from Abu Saʿid al-Khudri, who said regarding the saying of Allah ﴿a narrow livelihood﴾: it is the punishment of the grave.

- Muhammad ibn ʿAbd Allah ibn Bazi' narrated to me, saying: Bishr ibn al-Mufaddal narrated to us, saying: ʿAbd al-Rahman ibn Ishaq narrated to us, from Abu Hazim, from al-Nuʿman ibn Abi ʿAyyash, from Abu Saʿid al-Khudri, who said: The narrow livelihood about which Allah said is the punishment of the grave.

- Hawthara ibn Muhammad al-Minqari narrated to me, saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from Abu Hazim, from Abu Salamah, from Abu Saʿid al-Khudri ﴿indeed, he will have a narrow life﴾: he said: His grave is constricted for him until his ribs interlock.

- Muhammad ibn ʿAbd Allah ibn ʿAbd al-Hakam narrated to me, saying: My father and Shuʿayb ibn al-Layth narrated to us, from al-Layth, saying: Khalid ibn Zayd narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Hilal, from Abu Hazim, from Abu Saʿid, that he used to say: The narrow livelihood is the punishment of the grave. Indeed, ninety-nine serpents (tinnin) are set upon the disbeliever in his grave, biting him and scratching his flesh until he is resurrected. It used to be said: If one of those serpents breathed upon the earth, nothing would grow in it.

- Mujahid ibn Musa narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn ʿAmr narrated to us, from Abu Salamah, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The grave of the disbeliever is pressed upon until his ribs interlock, and this is the narrow livelihood about which Allah said ﴿a narrow livelihood, and We will gather him on the Day of Resurrection blind﴾.

- Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Jabir ibn Nuh narrated to us, from Isma'il ibn Abi Khalid, from Abu Salih and al-Suddi, regarding His saying ﴿a narrow livelihood﴾: he said: the punishment of the grave.

- Muhammad ibn Isma'il al-Ahmasi narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn ʿUbayd narrated to us, saying: Sufyan al-Thawri narrated to us, from Isma'il ibn Abi Khalid, from Abu Salih, regarding His saying ﴿indeed, he will have a narrow life﴾: he said: the punishment of the grave.

- ʿAbd al-Rahman ibn al-Aswad narrated to me, saying: Muhammad ibn Rabi'ah narrated to us, saying: Abu ʿUmays narrated to us, from ʿAbd Allah ibn Mukhariq, from his father, from ʿAbd Allah, regarding His saying ﴿a narrow livelihood﴾: he said: the punishment of the grave.

- ʿAbd al-Rahim al-Barqi narrated to me, saying: Ibn Abi Maryam narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Jaʿfar and Ibn Abi Hazim narrated to us, both saying: Abu Hazim narrated to us, from al-Nuʿman ibn Abi ʿAyyash, from Abu Saʿid al-Khudri, ﴿a narrow livelihood﴾: he said: the punishment of the grave.

Abu Jaʿfar (al-Tabari) said: The most correct of the sayings regarding this is the saying of the one who said: it is the punishment of the grave, which was narrated to us by Ahmad ibn ʿAbd al-Rahman ibn Wahb, saying: My paternal uncle ʿAbd Allah ibn Wahb narrated to us, saying: ʿAmr ibn al-Harith informed me, from Darraj, from Ibn Hujayrah, from Abu Hurayrah, from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) that he said: "Do you know for what this verse was revealed: ﴿indeed, he will have a narrow life, and We will gather him on the Day of Resurrection blind﴾? Do you know what the narrow livelihood is?" They said: "Allah and His Messenger know best." He said: "It is the punishment of the disbeliever in his grave. By Him in whose hand is my soul, indeed ninety-nine tinnin (serpents) will be set upon him. Do you know what the tinnin is? Ninety-nine snakes, each with seven heads, which will blow into his body, sting him and scratch him until the Day of Resurrection."

Allah, blessed and exalted, followed that with His saying: ﴿And the punishment of the Hereafter is more severe and more lasting﴾. It was thus known that the narrow livelihood which Allah placed for them is before the punishment of the Hereafter, because if that were in the Hereafter, His saying ﴿And the punishment of the Hereafter is more severe and more lasting﴾ would have no understood meaning, since if there were not a punishment for them before the Hereafter, so that the one in the Hereafter would be more severe than it, the meaning of His saying ﴿And the punishment of the Hereafter is more severe and more lasting﴾ would be void. Since that is so, that narrow livelihood which Allah placed for them is either in their life in this world, or in their graves before resurrection, as there is no sense in its being in the Hereafter for what we have explained. If it were in their life in this world, then it would necessarily follow that every disbeliever who turns away from the remembrance of Allah has a narrow livelihood, yet we find many of them with a wider livelihood than many of those who devote themselves to the remembrance of Allah, blessed and exalted, and who believe in it, which shows that this is not so. Since the explanation is free of these two aspects, the third aspect is correct, namely that it is in the barzakh.

* *

His saying ﴿and We will gather him on the Day of Resurrection blind﴾

The interpreters differed regarding the nature of the blindness which Allah mentioned in this verse, with which He resurrects these disbelievers on the Day of Resurrection. Some of them said: That is blindness to the proof, not blindness of sight.

Those who said that:

- Muhammad ibn Isma'il al-Ahmasi narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn ʿUbayd narrated to us, saying: Sufyan al-Thawri narrated to us, from Isma'il ibn Abi Khalid, from Abu Salih, regarding His saying ﴿and We will gather him on the Day of Resurrection blind﴾: he said: He has no proof.

- Muhammad ibn ʿAmr narrated to me, saying: Abu ʿAsim narrated to us, saying: ʿIsa narrated to us, and al-Harith narrated to me, saying: al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Warqa' narrated to us, all from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His saying ﴿and We will gather him on the Day of Resurrection blind﴾: he said: from the proof.

- al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujahid, the like of it. It was also said: He is gathered blind in sight.

Abu Jaʿfar said: The correct statement on this is what Allah, mighty and remembered, said, namely that he is gathered blind to the proof and to seeing things, as He, may His praise be exalted, informed, and He made it general and did not restrict it.

* *

His saying ﴿He will say, "My Lord, why have You gathered me blind, while I had been seeing?"﴾

The interpreters differed regarding the interpretation of this. Some of them said, regarding it:

- Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: ʿAbd al-Razzaq narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding ﴿He will say, "My Lord, why have You gathered me blind"﴾: "I have no proof."

* *

His saying ﴿while I had been seeing﴾

The interpreters differed regarding its interpretation. Some of them said: its meaning is: while I had been seeing with my proof.

Those who said that: al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujahid, regarding ﴿while I had been seeing﴾: he said: knowing with my proof.

Others said: Rather, its meaning is: while I had been one with sight by which I perceived things.

Those who said that:

- Muhammad ibn ʿAmr narrated to me, saying: Abu ʿAsim narrated to us, saying: ʿIsa narrated to us, and al-Harith narrated to me, saying: al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Warqa' narrated to us, all from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding ﴿while I had been seeing﴾: in the world.

- Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding His saying ﴿He will say, "My Lord, why have You gathered me blind, while I had been seeing"﴾: he said: he had far sight and short vision, blind to the truth.

Abu Jaʿfar said: The correct statement on this in our view is that Allah, mighty of affair and majestic of praise, made it general in informing of him by describing himself with sight, and did not restrict any meaning over another; so it stands as He made it general. Given that, the interpretation of the verse is: "My Lord, why have You gathered me blind to my proof and to seeing things, when in the world I had sight in all of that."

If someone says: How did he say this to his Lord, "why have You gathered me blind," while witnessing the greatness of His authority? Did he not know in that place that it is for Allah to do with him what He wills? Or what is the meaning of this? It is said: This is a request from him to his Lord, that He make known to him the crime for which he deserved this, since he had been ignorant of it and thought he had no crime that merited this from Him. So he said: "My Lord, for what sin and what crime have You gathered me blind, when I had been seeing before in the world, and You do not punish anyone except less than what he deserves from You in punishment."

* *

His saying ﴿He will say, "Thus Our signs came to you, but you forgot them"﴾

His, may He be exalted and remembered, says: Allah then says to the one who said to Him: "Why have You gathered me blind, when I had been seeing?": I did this to you; I gathered you blind just as My signs came to you, which are My proofs and evidences and the clarification which I made clear in My Book, but you forgot them: meaning, you left them and turned away from them, did not believe in them, and did not act upon them. By His saying ﴿Thus it came to you﴾ He means: thus it came to you.

* *

His saying: ﴿And thus today you are forgotten﴾

He says: Just as you forgot Our signs in the world, leaving them and turning away from them, so today We forget you, and leave you in the Fire.

The interpreters differed regarding the meaning of His saying ﴿And thus today you are forgotten﴾. Some of them said the like of what we have said about it.

Those who said that:

- Muhammad ibn Isma'il al-Ahmasi narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn ʿUbayd narrated to us, saying: Sufyan al-Thawri narrated to us, from Isma'il ibn Abi Khalid, from Abu Salih, regarding His saying ﴿And thus today you are forgotten﴾: he said: in the Fire.

- al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: ʿAbd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Maʿmar informed us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His saying ﴿Thus Our signs came to you, but you forgot them﴾: he said: you left them, ﴿And thus today you are forgotten﴾: and thus today you are left in the Fire.

It was narrated from Qatadah regarding this what follows:

- Bishr narrated to me, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding His saying ﴿He said, "Thus Our signs came to you, but you forgot them, and thus today you are forgotten"﴾: he said: he forgot the good, and did not forget the evil. This saying of Qatadah is close in meaning to what Abu Salih and Mujahid said, because His leaving them in the Fire is the greatest evil for them.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 20, verses 124–126:

The interpretation of His, may He be exalted, saying: ﴿And whoever turns away from My remembrance, indeed he will have a narrow life, and We will gather him on the Day of Resurrection blind. He will say, "My Lord, why have You gathered me blind, while I had been seeing?" He will say, "Thus Our signs came to you, but you forgot them; and thus today you are forgotten."﴾

His, may He be exalted and remembered, says: ﴿And whoever turns away from My remembrance﴾, meaning the reminder with which I remind him, so he turns away from it, does not accept it, does not respond to it, and is not admonished by it, so that he refrains from what he persists in of disobedience to his Lord's command. ﴿Indeed, he will have a narrow life﴾ means: indeed, he will have a constricted life. The word ḍank (narrow, straitened) applied to dwellings, places and livelihoods means severe: one says, "This is a ḍank dwelling" when it is cramped, and "ʿaysh ḍank" (a straitened life). The masculine and feminine, the singular and dual and plural, are used with one form. From it is the saying of ʿAntarah:

"And if they alight in a ḍank place, I alight (with them)."
[[This is part of the second half of a verse by ʿAntarah ibn ʿAmr ibn Shaddad al-ʿAbsi (Mukhtar al-Shiʿr al-Jahili, al-Halabi edition, sharh Mustafa al-Saqqa, p. 388). The full verse is: "If they are overtaken, I charge; if they are pressed in battle, I hold firm; and if they are found in a ḍank place, I alight."]]

And in Lisan (entry ḍ-n-k): ḍank means narrowness of anything; the masculine and feminine are alike in it. A ḍank livelihood is a constricted one. In the Revelation: "Indeed, he will have a narrow life," i.e., not lawful.

Those who interpret the Qur'an said what we have said in this regard.

Those who said that:

- Ali narrated to me, saying: ʿAbd Allah narrated to us, saying: Muʿawiyah narrated to me, from ʿAli, from Ibn ʿAbbas, regarding His saying ﴿indeed, he will have a narrow life﴾: he says: wretchedness.

- Muhammad ibn ʿAmr narrated to me, saying: Abu ʿAsim narrated to us, saying: ʿIsa narrated to us, and al-Harith narrated to me, saying: al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Warqa' narrated to us, all from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His saying ﴿ḍankan﴾: he said: constricted.

- al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: ʿAbd al-Razzaq narrated to us, from Maʿmar, from Qatadah, regarding His saying ﴿indeed, he will have a narrow life﴾: he said: The ḍank is the narrowness.

- Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Hakkam narrated to us, from ʿAnbasah, from Muhammad ibn ʿAbd al-Rahman, from al-Qasim ibn Abi Bazzah, from Mujahid, regarding His saying ﴿indeed, he will have a narrow life﴾: he says: constricted.

- al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujahid, the like of it.

The interpreters differed regarding the place where Allah placed for those who turn away from His remembrance the narrow life, and the state in which He placed them. Some of them said: He placed it for them in the Hereafter, in Hell, because their food there is ḍarīʿ and zaqqum.

Those who said that:

- Muhammad ibn ʿAmr ibn ʿAli ibn Muqaddam narrated to me, saying: Yahya ibn Saʿid narrated to us, from ʿAwf, from al-Hasan, regarding His saying: ﴿indeed, he will have a narrow life﴾: he said: in Hell.

- Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His saying ﴿And whoever turns away from My remembrance, indeed he will have a narrow life﴾, then he recited until he reached ﴿and does not believe in the signs of his Lord﴾, and said: These are the people of disbelief. He said: As for a narrow life, in the Fire there are thorns of fire, zaqqum and ghislin, and the ḍarīʿ is a thorn of fire. There is no livelihood in the grave or in this world; livelihood and life are only in the Hereafter. He recited the saying of Allah, mighty and majestic: ﴿Would that I had sent ahead for my life﴾ and said: "for my livelihood." He said: The ghislin and zaqqum are things that the people of this world do not know.

- al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: ʿAbd al-Razzaq narrated to us, from Maʿmar, from Qatadah: ﴿indeed, he will have a narrow life﴾: he said: in the Fire.

Others said: Rather, He meant by it: indeed, he will have a livelihood in this world that is unlawful. He said: Allah, mighty and majestic, described their livelihood as narrow, because unlawful wealth, even if it is abundant, is narrow.

Those who said that:

- Muhammad ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Yahya ibn Wadih narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn ibn Waqid narrated to us, from Yazid, from ʿIkrimah, regarding His saying: ﴿a narrow livelihood﴾: he said: It is the livelihood in which Allah gave him abundance from the unlawful.

- Dawud ibn Sulayman ibn Yazid al-Mukatib, from the people of Basra, narrated to me, saying: ʿAmr ibn Jarir al-Bajali narrated to us, from Isma'il ibn Abi Khalid, from Qays ibn Abi Hazim, regarding the saying of Allah ﴿a narrow livelihood﴾: he said: a provision in disobedience to Him.

- ʿAbd al-ʿAla ibn Wasil narrated to me, saying: Yaʿla ibn ʿUbayd narrated to us, saying: Abu Bistam narrated to us, from al-Dahhak, ﴿indeed, he will have a narrow life﴾: he said: the evil earning.

- Muhammad ibn Isma'il al-Sarrari narrated to me, saying: Muhammad ibn Sawwar narrated to us, saying: Abu al-Yaqzan ʿAmmar ibn Muhammad narrated to us, from Harun ibn Muhammad al-Taymi, from al-Dahhak, regarding His saying ﴿indeed, he will have a narrow life﴾: he said: the evil deed and the bad provision.

Others, among those who said that He meant that these people have a narrow life in this world, said: It is only called narrow although it is wide, because they spend what they spend of their wealth while disbelieving in Allah's replacement and despairing of Allah's bounty, and having an evil opinion of their Lord; so their livelihood becomes harsh and constricted for them because of that.

Those who said that:

- Muhammad ibn Saʿd narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, saying: My paternal uncle narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn ʿAbbas, regarding His saying ﴿And whoever turns away from My remembrance, indeed he will have a narrow life﴾: he says: Every wealth I give to a servant of Mine, whether little or much, in which he does not fear Me, has no good in it, and it is the narrowness in livelihood. It is said that some astray people turned away from the truth, and they were people of abundance and wealth in this world, but their livelihood was narrow. That is because they used to think that Allah, mighty and majestic, would not replace their livelihoods, out of their evil opinion of Allah and their denial of Him. When a servant denies Allah and has an evil opinion of Him, his livelihood becomes harsh upon him, and that is the ḍank.

Others said: Rather, He meant by it: that this is for them in the barzakh, which is the punishment of the grave.

Those who said that:

- Yazid ibn Makhlad al-Wasiti narrated to me, saying: Khalid ibn ʿAbd Allah narrated to us, from ʿAbd al-Rahman ibn Ishaq, from Abu Hazim, from al-Nuʿman ibn Abi ʿAyyash, from Abu Saʿid al-Khudri, who said regarding the saying of Allah ﴿a narrow livelihood﴾: it is the punishment of the grave.

- Muhammad ibn ʿAbd Allah ibn Bazi' narrated to me, saying: Bishr ibn al-Mufaddal narrated to us, saying: ʿAbd al-Rahman ibn Ishaq narrated to us, from Abu Hazim, from al-Nuʿman ibn Abi ʿAyyash, from Abu Saʿid al-Khudri, who said: The narrow livelihood about which Allah said is the punishment of the grave.

- Hawthara ibn Muhammad al-Minqari narrated to me, saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from Abu Hazim, from Abu Salamah, from Abu Saʿid al-Khudri ﴿indeed, he will have a narrow life﴾: he said: His grave is constricted for him until his ribs interlock.

- Muhammad ibn ʿAbd Allah ibn ʿAbd al-Hakam narrated to me, saying: My father and Shuʿayb ibn al-Layth narrated to us, from al-Layth, saying: Khalid ibn Zayd narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Hilal, from Abu Hazim, from Abu Saʿid, that he used to say: The narrow livelihood is the punishment of the grave. Indeed, ninety-nine serpents (tinnin) are set upon the disbeliever in his grave, biting him and scratching his flesh until he is resurrected. It used to be said: If one of those serpents breathed upon the earth, nothing would grow in it.

- Mujahid ibn Musa narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn ʿAmr narrated to us, from Abu Salamah, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The grave of the disbeliever is pressed upon until his ribs interlock, and this is the narrow livelihood about which Allah said ﴿a narrow livelihood, and We will gather him on the Day of Resurrection blind﴾.

- Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Jabir ibn Nuh narrated to us, from Isma'il ibn Abi Khalid, from Abu Salih and al-Suddi, regarding His saying ﴿a narrow livelihood﴾: he said: the punishment of the grave.

- Muhammad ibn Isma'il al-Ahmasi narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn ʿUbayd narrated to us, saying: Sufyan al-Thawri narrated to us, from Isma'il ibn Abi Khalid, from Abu Salih, regarding His saying ﴿indeed, he will have a narrow life﴾: he said: the punishment of the grave.

- ʿAbd al-Rahman ibn al-Aswad narrated to me, saying: Muhammad ibn Rabi'ah narrated to us, saying: Abu ʿUmays narrated to us, from ʿAbd Allah ibn Mukhariq, from his father, from ʿAbd Allah, regarding His saying ﴿a narrow livelihood﴾: he said: the punishment of the grave.

- ʿAbd al-Rahim al-Barqi narrated to me, saying: Ibn Abi Maryam narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Jaʿfar and Ibn Abi Hazim narrated to us, both saying: Abu Hazim narrated to us, from al-Nuʿman ibn Abi ʿAyyash, from Abu Saʿid al-Khudri, ﴿a narrow livelihood﴾: he said: the punishment of the grave.

Abu Jaʿfar (al-Tabari) said: The most correct of the sayings regarding this is the saying of the one who said: it is the punishment of the grave, which was narrated to us by Ahmad ibn ʿAbd al-Rahman ibn Wahb, saying: My paternal uncle ʿAbd Allah ibn Wahb narrated to us, saying: ʿAmr ibn al-Harith informed me, from Darraj, from Ibn Hujayrah, from Abu Hurayrah, from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) that he said: "Do you know for what this verse was revealed: ﴿indeed, he will have a narrow life, and We will gather him on the Day of Resurrection blind﴾? Do you know what the narrow livelihood is?" They said: "Allah and His Messenger know best." He said: "It is the punishment of the disbeliever in his grave. By Him in whose hand is my soul, indeed ninety-nine tinnin (serpents) will be set upon him. Do you know what the tinnin is? Ninety-nine snakes, each with seven heads, which will blow into his body, sting him and scratch him until the Day of Resurrection."

Allah, blessed and exalted, followed that with His saying: ﴿And the punishment of the Hereafter is more severe and more lasting﴾. It was thus known that the narrow livelihood which Allah placed for them is before the punishment of the Hereafter, because if that were in the Hereafter, His saying ﴿And the punishment of the Hereafter is more severe and more lasting﴾ would have no understood meaning, since if there were not a punishment for them before the Hereafter, so that the one in the Hereafter would be more severe than it, the meaning of His saying ﴿And the punishment of the Hereafter is more severe and more lasting﴾ would be void. Since that is so, that narrow livelihood which Allah placed for them is either in their life in this world, or in their graves before resurrection, as there is no sense in its being in the Hereafter for what we have explained. If it were in their life in this world, then it would necessarily follow that every disbeliever who turns away from the remembrance of Allah has a narrow livelihood, yet we find many of them with a wider livelihood than many of those who devote themselves to the remembrance of Allah, blessed and exalted, and who believe in it, which shows that this is not so. Since the explanation is free of these two aspects, the third aspect is correct, namely that it is in the barzakh.

* *

His saying ﴿and We will gather him on the Day of Resurrection blind﴾

The interpreters differed regarding the nature of the blindness which Allah mentioned in this verse, with which He resurrects these disbelievers on the Day of Resurrection. Some of them said: That is blindness to the proof, not blindness of sight.

Those who said that:

- Muhammad ibn Isma'il al-Ahmasi narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn ʿUbayd narrated to us, saying: Sufyan al-Thawri narrated to us, from Isma'il ibn Abi Khalid, from Abu Salih, regarding His saying ﴿and We will gather him on the Day of Resurrection blind﴾: he said: He has no proof.

- Muhammad ibn ʿAmr narrated to me, saying: Abu ʿAsim narrated to us, saying: ʿIsa narrated to us, and al-Harith narrated to me, saying: al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Warqa' narrated to us, all from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His saying ﴿and We will gather him on the Day of Resurrection blind﴾: he said: from the proof.

- al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujahid, the like of it. It was also said: He is gathered blind in sight.

Abu Jaʿfar said: The correct statement on this is what Allah, mighty and remembered, said, namely that he is gathered blind to the proof and to seeing things, as He, may His praise be exalted, informed, and He made it general and did not restrict it.

* *

His saying ﴿He will say, "My Lord, why have You gathered me blind, while I had been seeing?"﴾

The interpreters differed regarding the interpretation of this. Some of them said, regarding it:

- Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: ʿAbd al-Razzaq narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding ﴿He will say, "My Lord, why have You gathered me blind"﴾: "I have no proof."

* *

His saying ﴿while I had been seeing﴾

The interpreters differed regarding its interpretation. Some of them said: its meaning is: while I had been seeing with my proof.

Those who said that: al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujahid, regarding ﴿while I had been seeing﴾: he said: knowing with my proof.

Others said: Rather, its meaning is: while I had been one with sight by which I perceived things.

Those who said that:

- Muhammad ibn ʿAmr narrated to me, saying: Abu ʿAsim narrated to us, saying: ʿIsa narrated to us, and al-Harith narrated to me, saying: al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Warqa' narrated to us, all from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding ﴿while I had been seeing﴾: in the world.

- Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding His saying ﴿He will say, "My Lord, why have You gathered me blind, while I had been seeing"﴾: he said: he had far sight and short vision, blind to the truth.

Abu Jaʿfar said: The correct statement on this in our view is that Allah, mighty of affair and majestic of praise, made it general in informing of him by describing himself with sight, and did not restrict any meaning over another; so it stands as He made it general. Given that, the interpretation of the verse is: "My Lord, why have You gathered me blind to my proof and to seeing things, when in the world I had sight in all of that."

If someone says: How did he say this to his Lord, "why have You gathered me blind," while witnessing the greatness of His authority? Did he not know in that place that it is for Allah to do with him what He wills? Or what is the meaning of this? It is said: This is a request from him to his Lord, that He make known to him the crime for which he deserved this, since he had been ignorant of it and thought he had no crime that merited this from Him. So he said: "My Lord, for what sin and what crime have You gathered me blind, when I had been seeing before in the world, and You do not punish anyone except less than what he deserves from You in punishment."

* *

His saying ﴿He will say, "Thus Our signs came to you, but you forgot them"﴾

His, may He be exalted and remembered, says: Allah then says to the one who said to Him: "Why have You gathered me blind, when I had been seeing?": I did this to you; I gathered you blind just as My signs came to you, which are My proofs and evidences and the clarification which I made clear in My Book, but you forgot them: meaning, you left them and turned away from them, did not believe in them, and did not act upon them. By His saying ﴿Thus it came to you﴾ He means: thus it came to you.

* *

His saying: ﴿And thus today you are forgotten﴾

He says: Just as you forgot Our signs in the world, leaving them and turning away from them, so today We forget you, and leave you in the Fire.

The interpreters differed regarding the meaning of His saying ﴿And thus today you are forgotten﴾. Some of them said the like of what we have said about it.

Those who said that:

- Muhammad ibn Isma'il al-Ahmasi narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn ʿUbayd narrated to us, saying: Sufyan al-Thawri narrated to us, from Isma'il ibn Abi Khalid, from Abu Salih, regarding His saying ﴿And thus today you are forgotten﴾: he said: in the Fire.

- al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: ʿAbd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Maʿmar informed us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His saying ﴿Thus Our signs came to you, but you forgot them﴾: he said: you left them, ﴿And thus today you are forgotten﴾: and thus today you are left in the Fire.

It was narrated from Qatadah regarding this what follows:

- Bishr narrated to me, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding His saying ﴿He said, "Thus Our signs came to you, but you forgot them, and thus today you are forgotten"﴾: he said: he forgot the good, and did not forget the evil. This saying of Qatadah is close in meaning to what Abu Salih and Mujahid said, because His leaving them in the Fire is the greatest evil for them.

- Yazid ibn Makhlad al-Wasiti narrated to me, saying: Khalid ibn ʿAbd Allah narrated to us, from ʿAbd al-Rahman ibn Ishaq, from Abu Hazim, from al-Nuʿman ibn Abi ʿAyyash, from Abu Saʿid al-Khudri, who said regarding the saying of Allah ﴿a narrow livelihood﴾: it is the punishment of the grave.

- Muhammad ibn ʿAbd Allah ibn Bazi' narrated to me, saying: Bishr ibn al-Mufaddal narrated to us, saying: ʿAbd al-Rahman ibn Ishaq narrated to us, from Abu Hazim, from al-Nuʿman ibn Abi ʿAyyash, from Abu Saʿid al-Khudri, who said: The narrow livelihood about which Allah said is the punishment of the grave.

- Hawthara ibn Muhammad al-Minqari narrated to me, saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from Abu Hazim, from Abu Salamah, from Abu Saʿid al-Khudri ﴿indeed, he will have a narrow life﴾: he said: His grave is constricted for him until his ribs interlock.

- Muhammad ibn ʿAbd Allah ibn ʿAbd al-Hakam narrated to me, saying: My father and Shuʿayb ibn al-Layth narrated to us, from al-Layth, saying: Khalid ibn Zayd narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Hilal, from Abu Hazim, from Abu Saʿid, that he used to say: The narrow livelihood is the punishment of the grave. Indeed, ninety-nine serpents (tinnin) are set upon the disbeliever in his grave, biting him and scratching his flesh until he is resurrected. It used to be said: If one of those serpents breathed upon the earth, nothing would grow in it.

- Mujahid ibn Musa narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn ʿAmr narrated to us, from Abu Salamah, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The grave of the disbeliever is pressed upon until his ribs interlock, and this is the narrow livelihood about which Allah said ﴿a narrow livelihood, and We will gather him on the Day of Resurrection blind﴾.

- Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Jabir ibn Nuh narrated to us, from Isma'il ibn Abi Khalid, from Abu Salih and al-Suddi, regarding His saying ﴿a narrow livelihood﴾: he said: the punishment of the grave.

- Muhammad ibn Isma'il al-Ahmasi narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn ʿUbayd narrated to us, saying: Sufyan al-Thawri narrated to us, from Isma'il ibn Abi Khalid, from Abu Salih, regarding His saying ﴿indeed, he will have a narrow life﴾: he said: the punishment of the grave.

- ʿAbd al-Rahman ibn al-Aswad narrated to me, saying: Muhammad ibn Rabi'ah narrated to us, saying: Abu ʿUmays narrated to us, from ʿAbd Allah ibn Mukhariq, from his father, from ʿAbd Allah, regarding His saying ﴿a narrow livelihood﴾: he said: the punishment of the grave.

- ʿAbd al-Rahim al-Barqi narrated to me, saying: Ibn Abi Maryam narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Jaʿfar and Ibn Abi Hazim narrated to us, both saying: Abu Hazim narrated to us, from al-Nuʿman ibn Abi ʿAyyash, from Abu Saʿid al-Khudri, ﴿a narrow livelihood﴾: he said: the punishment of the grave.

Abu Jaʿfar (al-Tabari) said: The most correct of the sayings regarding this is the saying of the one who said: it is the punishment of the grave, which was narrated to us by Ahmad ibn ʿAbd al-Rahman ibn Wahb, saying: My paternal uncle ʿAbd Allah ibn Wahb narrated to us, saying: ʿAmr ibn al-Harith informed me, from Darraj, from Ibn Hujayrah, from Abu Hurayrah, from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) that he said: "Do you know for what this verse was revealed: ﴿indeed, he will have a narrow life, and We will gather him on the Day of Resurrection blind﴾? Do you know what the narrow livelihood is?" They said: "Allah and His Messenger know best." He said: "It is the punishment of the disbeliever in his grave. By Him in whose hand is my soul, indeed ninety-nine tinnin (serpents) will be set upon him. Do you know what the tinnin is? Ninety-nine snakes, each with seven heads, which will blow into his body, sting him and scratch him until the Day of Resurrection."

Allah, blessed and exalted, followed that with His saying: ﴿And the punishment of the Hereafter is more severe and more lasting﴾. It was thus known that the narrow livelihood which Allah placed for them is before the punishment of the Hereafter, because if that were in the Hereafter, His saying ﴿And the punishment of the Hereafter is more severe and more lasting﴾ would have no understood meaning, since if there were not a punishment for them before the Hereafter, so that the one in the Hereafter would be more severe than it, the meaning of His saying ﴿And the punishment of the Hereafter is more severe and more lasting﴾ would be void. Since that is so, that narrow livelihood which Allah placed for them is either in their life in this world, or in their graves before resurrection, as there is no sense in its being in the Hereafter for what we have explained. If it were in their life in this world, then it would necessarily follow that every disbeliever who turns away from the remembrance of Allah has a narrow livelihood, yet we find many of them with a wider livelihood than many of those who devote themselves to the remembrance of Allah, blessed and exalted, and who believe in it, which shows that this is not so. Since the explanation is free of these two aspects, the third aspect is correct, namely that it is in the barzakh.

* *

His saying ﴿and We will gather him on the Day of Resurrection blind﴾

The interpreters differed regarding the nature of the blindness which Allah mentioned in this verse, with which He resurrects these disbelievers on the Day of Resurrection. Some of them said: That is blindness to the proof, not blindness of sight.

Those who said that:

- Muhammad ibn Isma'il al-Ahmasi narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn ʿUbayd narrated to us, saying: Sufyan al-Thawri narrated to us, from Isma'il ibn Abi Khalid, from Abu Salih, regarding His saying ﴿and We will gather him on the Day of Resurrection blind﴾: he said: He has no proof.

- Muhammad ibn ʿAmr narrated to me, saying: Abu ʿAsim narrated to us, saying: ʿIsa narrated to us, and al-Harith narrated to me, saying: al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Warqa' narrated to us, all from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His saying ﴿and We will gather him on the Day of Resurrection blind﴾: he said: from the proof.

- al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujahid, the like of it. It was also said: He is gathered blind in sight.

Abu Jaʿfar said: The correct statement on this is what Allah, mighty and remembered, said, namely that he is gathered blind to the proof and to seeing things, as He, may His praise be exalted, informed, and He made it general and did not restrict it.

* *

His saying ﴿He will say, "My Lord, why have You gathered me blind, while I had been seeing?"﴾

The interpreters differed regarding the interpretation of this. Some of them said, regarding it:

- Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: ʿAbd al-Razzaq narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding ﴿He will say, "My Lord, why have You gathered me blind"﴾: "I have no proof."

* *

His saying ﴿while I had been seeing﴾

The interpreters differed regarding its interpretation. Some of them said: its meaning is: while I had been seeing with my proof.

Those who said that: al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujahid, regarding ﴿while I had been seeing﴾: he said: knowing with my proof.

Others said: Rather, its meaning is: while I had been one with sight by which I perceived things.

Those who said that:

- Muhammad ibn ʿAmr narrated to me, saying: Abu ʿAsim narrated to us, saying: ʿIsa narrated to us, and al-Harith narrated to me, saying: al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Warqa' narrated to us, all from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding ﴿while I had been seeing﴾: in the world.

- Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding His saying ﴿He will say, "My Lord, why have You gathered me blind, while I had been seeing"﴾: he said: he had far sight and short vision, blind to the truth.

Abu Jaʿfar said: The correct statement on this in our view is that Allah, mighty of affair and majestic of praise, made it general in informing of him by describing himself with sight, and did not restrict any meaning over another; so it stands as He made it general. Given that, the interpretation of the verse is: "My Lord, why have You gathered me blind to my proof and to seeing things, when in the world I had sight in all of that."

If someone says: How did he say this to his Lord, "why have You gathered me blind," while witnessing the greatness of His authority? Did he not know in that place that it is for Allah to do with him what He wills? Or what is the meaning of this? It is said: This is a request from him to his Lord, that He make known to him the crime for which he deserved this, since he had been ignorant of it and thought he had no crime that merited this from Him. So he said: "My Lord, for what sin and what crime have You gathered me blind, when I had been seeing before in the world, and You do not punish anyone except less than what he deserves from You in punishment."

* *

His saying ﴿He will say, "Thus Our signs came to you, but you forgot them"﴾

His, may He be exalted and remembered, says: Allah then says to the one who said to Him: "Why have You gathered me blind, when I had been seeing?": I did this to you; I gathered you blind just as My signs came to you, which are My proofs and evidences and the clarification which I made clear in My Book, but you forgot them: meaning, you left them and turned away from them, did not believe in them, and did not act upon them. By His saying ﴿Thus it came to you﴾ He means: thus it came to you.

* *

His saying: ﴿And thus today you are forgotten﴾

He says: Just as you forgot Our signs in the world, leaving them and turning away from them, so today We forget you, and leave you in the Fire.

The interpreters differed regarding the meaning of His saying ﴿And thus today you are forgotten﴾. Some of them said the like of what we have said about it.

Those who said that:

- Muhammad ibn Isma'il al-Ahmasi narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn ʿUbayd narrated to us, saying: Sufyan al-Thawri narrated to us, from Isma'il ibn Abi Khalid, from Abu Salih, regarding His saying ﴿And thus today you are forgotten﴾: he said: in the Fire.

- al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: ʿAbd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Maʿmar informed us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His saying ﴿Thus Our signs came to you, but you forgot them﴾: he said: you left them, ﴿And thus today you are forgotten﴾: and thus today you are left in the Fire.

It was narrated from Qatadah regarding this what follows:

- Bishr narrated to me, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding His saying ﴿He said, "Thus Our signs came to you, but you forgot them, and thus today you are forgotten"﴾: he said: he forgot the good, and did not forget the evil. This saying of Qatadah is close in meaning to what Abu Salih and Mujahid said, because His leaving them in the Fire is the greatest evil for them.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 20, verses 127–128:

The interpretation of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And thus do We recompense him who transgresses and does not believe in the signs of his Lord. And the punishment of the Hereafter is more severe and more lasting (127)﴾

He, exalted is His mention, says: "And thus do We recompense," meaning: We reward whoever transgresses and disobeys his Lord and does not believe in His messengers and His books, so We will make for him a straitened life in the barzakh (the intermediate state), as We have already explained earlier. ﴿And the punishment of the Hereafter is more severe and more lasting﴾: He, may His praise be exalted, says: the punishment in the Hereafter is more severe for them than what I promised them in the grave of straitened life, and "more lasting" means: more enduring than it, because it has no appointed end and no termination.

* *

The interpretation of His saying: ﴿Does it not guide them how many generations We destroyed before them, among whose dwellings they walk? Indeed, in that are signs for people of intellect (128)﴾

He, exalted is His mention, says to His Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ): "Does it not guide your people, the polytheists who associate others with Allah?" The meaning of yahdi (guide) is: makes clear. He says: Has it not made clear to them how many of the nations We destroyed before them, whose dwellings they walk through, and see the traces of Our punishments that We brought down upon them, the evil consequence of what they persist in of disbelief in Our signs, so that they may take warning from them, take lesson, turn back to submission, and believe in Allah and His Messenger, fearing that what befell them for their disbelief in Allah may befall them too?

Similar to what we have said regarding this, the people of interpretation (ahl al-ta'wil) have said.

Mention of those who said so:

Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid related to us, saying: Sa'id related to us, from Qatadah, regarding His saying ﴿how many generations We destroyed before them, among whose dwellings they walk﴾: because the Quraysh used to trade to Syria, passing by the dwellings of 'Ad, Thamud and those like them, and they saw the traces of Allah's punishments upon them. So He said to them: Has what they see of Our dealings with them for their disbelief in Us not warned them that the like of it may descend upon them, while they persist in the same deeds?

Al-Farra' used to say: it is not permissible for kam in this place to be anything but in the accusative case governed by ahlaknا. He used to say: although it is only accusative, the whole clause is in the nominative by His saying ﴿yahdi lahum﴾. He would say: this is like the speaker's saying, "It has become clear to me whether 'Amr or Zayd remained," in the interrogative sense, and like His saying ﴿It is the same for you whether you call them or you are silent﴾. He claims that there is something in it that makes sawa' nominative, which does not appear with the interrogative. He said: If you said, "sawa' 'alaykum sumtukum wa du'a'ukum," the nominative in the clause would be clear. But what al-Farra' said is not so, because kam, although it is one of the interrogative particles, is not used here for interrogation; rather it stands in the position of relative nouns (al-asma' al-mawsufa), and the meaning of the sentence is what we mentioned before: Has it not made clear to them how many of the generations We destroyed before them, through whose dwellings they walk? Or: have not the destroyed generations guided them? It has been reported that in the reading of 'Abdullah it is ﴿Afalam yahdi lahum man ahlakna﴾, so kam stands in the position of man in the reading of 'Abdullah, and it is in the nominative place governed by ﴿yahdi lahum﴾. This is the most apparent of its aspects and the most sound of its meanings, although what he said is a possibility and a view, though a remote one.

* *

As for His saying ﴿Indeed, in that are signs for people of intellect﴾:

He, exalted is His mention, says: Indeed, in what these people observe and see of the traces of Our dealings with the nations that denied their messengers before them, and the descent of Our exemplary punishments upon them for their disbelief in Allah, there are ﴿signs﴾, meaning: proofs, lessons and admonitions, ﴿for people of intellect﴾, meaning: for people of reason and understanding, and those whose intellect, understanding and religion restrain them from committing what harms them.

Similar to what we have said regarding this, the people of interpretation have said.

Mention of those who said so:

Ali narrated to me, saying: Abu Salih related to us, saying: Mu'awiyah related to me, from Ali, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding His saying ﴿for people of intellect (ulī al-nuhā)﴾: he said: "al-tuqa" (the pious).

Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid related to us, saying: Sa'id related to us, from Qatadah, regarding His saying ﴿Indeed, in that are signs for people of intellect﴾: "people of scrupulousness (ahl al-wara')."

The interpretation of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And thus do We recompense him who transgresses and does not believe in the signs of his Lord. And the punishment of the Hereafter is more severe and more lasting (127)﴾

* *
