Similar to what we have said regarding this, the people of interpretation have said.

Mention of those who said so:

Ali narrated to me, saying: Abu Salih related to us, saying: Mu'awiyah related to me, from Ali, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding His saying ﴿for people of intellect (ulī al-nuhā)﴾: he said: "al-tuqa" (the pious).

Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid related to us, saying: Sa'id related to us, from Qatadah, regarding His saying ﴿Indeed, in that are signs for people of intellect﴾: "people of scrupulousness (ahl al-wara')."

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 20, verses 129–130:

The interpretation of His saying, ﴿Had it not been for a word that preceded from your Lord, it would have been inevitable, and a specified term﴾ (129) ﴿So be patient over what they say, and glorify the praise of your Lord before the rising of the sun and before its setting, and during the hours of the night glorify Him, and at the ends of the day, that you may be pleased﴾ (130).

He, may He be remembered, says: ﴿Had it not been for a word that preceded from your Lord﴾, O Muhammad, that everyone for whom He has decreed a term, He will not seize before reaching his term. ﴿And a specified term﴾ means: and an appointed time with your Lord which He has named for them in the Mother of the Book and inscribed in it, which they will surely reach and fulfil. ﴿It would have been inevitable﴾ means: destruction would have been inevitable for them, immediately. It is a verbal noun from the saying of the speaker: "Fulan lazima Fulanan yalazimuhu mulazamatan wa lizaman," meaning: he did not part from him. He placed His saying ﴿it would have been inevitable﴾ before His saying ﴿a specified term﴾. The meaning of the speech is: Had it not been for a word that preceded from your Lord and a specified term, it would have been inevitable, so be patient over what they say.

And the exegetes said things similar to what we have said regarding this.

Those who said that:

Muhammad ibn Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu Asim told us, saying: Isa told us; and al-Harith narrated to me, saying: al-Hasan told us, saying: Warqa' told us, all of them from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His saying ﴿Had it not been for a word that preceded from your Lord, it would have been inevitable, and a specified term﴾: the specified term is the world.

Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid told us, saying: Sa'id told us, from Qatadah, regarding His saying ﴿Had it not been for a word that preceded from your Lord, it would have been inevitable, and a specified term﴾. And this is from the inverted order of speech; He says: Had it not been that a word preceded from your Lord to [[He may mean: had it not been that God's word preceded with the postponement of their punishment to a specified term. It is possible that "ila" (to) was placed in the position of the conjunction waw by a scribe's error.]] a specified term, it would have been inevitable. The specified term is the Hour, for God, may He be exalted, says: ﴿Nay, the Hour is their appointed promise, and the Hour is more calamitous and bitter﴾.

Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His saying ﴿Had it not been for a word that preceded from your Lord, it would have been inevitable, and a specified term﴾: This is inverted and postponed; the meaning is: Had it not been for a word that preceded from your Lord and a specified term, it would have been inevitable.

The exegetes differed regarding the meaning of His saying ﴿it would have been inevitable﴾. Some of them said: its meaning is: it would have been death.

Those who said that:

Ali narrated to me, saying: Abu Salih told me, saying: Mu'awiyah told me, from Ali, from Ibn Abbas, regarding His saying ﴿it would have been inevitable﴾: he says: death.

Others said: its meaning is: it would have been killing.

Those who said that:

Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said ﴿it would have been inevitable﴾, and the inevitability is killing.

* *

As for His saying ﴿So be patient over what they say﴾:

His majestic praise says to His Prophet: Be patient, O Muhammad, over what these deniers of God's signs from your people say to you, that you are a sorcerer, that you are a madman and a poet, and similar sayings. ﴿And glorify the praise of your Lord﴾ means: join your thanksgiving to your Lord, and He said "bi-hamdi rabbika" (with the praise of your Lord), and the meaning is "bi-hamdika rabbaka" (your praise of your Lord), just as you say: "a'jabani darb Zayd" (the striking of Zayd pleased me), meaning "darbi Zaydan" (my striking of Zayd). As for His saying ﴿before the rising of the sun﴾, that is the dawn prayer; ﴿and before its setting﴾, and it is the afternoon prayer; ﴿and during the hours of the night﴾, and they are the hours of the night, its singular being "ini", according to the pattern "hamil", and from it is the saying of al-Mutanakhkhil al-Sa'di:

Sweet and bitter, like the bending of an arrow-shaft is its bitterness,
in every hour of the night that it has passed, it puts on its sandals.

[[(In Lisan: anā) "lani" is the singular of "anā' al-layl", which are its hours; and in the revealed Book: "wa min anā'i al-layli" (and during the hours of the night). The people of language, among them al-Zajjaj, said: "anā' al-layl" are its hours, and its singular is "ini" and "inī"; whoever says "ini" it is like "nahā" and "anhā'"; and whoever says "ini" it is like "ma'ī" and "am'ā'"; al-Hudhali al-Mutanakhkhil said: "al-salik al-thaghra makhshiyyan mawaridahu / bi-kulli ini qadāhu al-layl yantali"*. Al-Azhari said: Ibn al-Anbari narrated it thus, and al-Jawhari recited the verse "Sweet and bitter..." and attributed it also to al-Mutanakhkhil; so either it is the verse he means, or another from a different poem.]]

And by His saying ﴿and during the hours of the night glorify Him﴾ He means the night prayer of 'isha', because it is performed after hours of the night have passed.

* *

As for His saying ﴿and at the ends of the day﴾:

It means the noon and sunset prayers. It was said: "ends of the day" refers to the two prayers that have been mentioned, because the noon prayer is at the end of the first end of the day and at the beginning of the second end of the day, so it lies at both ends; and the third end is the setting of the sun, at which the sunset prayer is performed; therefore it was said "ends" (atraf). It may be said that the two ends of the day are meant. It was also said "atraf", as it was said ﴿your hearts have inclined﴾ in the plural, while two hearts are meant; so the beginning of the second end and the end of the first end would be meant [[In the original: "al-akhir"? This is a scribal error, as is clear from the author's phrasing.]].

And the exegetes said things similar to what we have said regarding this.

Those who said that:

Muhammad ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Rahman told us, saying: Sufyan told us, from Asim, from Ibn Abi Zayd, from Ibn Abbas, regarding ﴿Glorify the praise of your Lord before the rising of the sun and before its setting﴾: he said: the obligatory prayer.

Tamim ibn al-Muntasir narrated to us, saying: Yazid ibn Harun told us, saying: Isma'il ibn Abi Khalid informed us, from Qays ibn Abi Hazim, from Jarir ibn Abd Allah, who said: We were sitting with the Messenger of God (ﷺ), and he looked at the moon on the night of the full moon and said: "Indeed you will see your Lord as you see this, you will not be wronged in seeing Him. So if you are able not to be overcome in a prayer before the rising of the sun and before its setting, then do it." Then he recited ﴿Glorify the praise of your Lord before the rising of the sun and before its setting﴾.

Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn told us, saying: Hajjaj told me, regarding ﴿Glorify the praise of your Lord before the rising of the sun and before its setting﴾: Ibn Jurayj said: the afternoon prayer; and "ends of the day": he said: the obligatory prayer.

Al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Razzaq informed us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah regarding His saying ﴿Glorify the praise of your Lord before the rising of the sun﴾: he said: it is the dawn prayer; ﴿and before its setting﴾: he said: the afternoon prayer; ﴿and during the hours of the night﴾: he said: the sunset and night prayers; ﴿and at the ends of the day﴾: he said: the noon prayer.

Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His saying ﴿and during the hours of the night glorify Him and at the ends of the day﴾: he said: "from the hours of the night": the 'atama (night prayer); "the ends of the day": the sunset and dawn prayers. The phrase ﴿and at the ends of the day﴾ is put in the accusative as a conjunction to His saying ﴿before the rising of the sun﴾, because the meaning is: glorify your Lord with praise at the end of the night and at the ends of the day.

And the exegetes said things similar to what we have said regarding the meaning of ﴿hours of the night﴾.

Those who said that:

Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn told us, saying: Hajjaj told me, from Ibn Jurayj, who said: Ibn Abbas said ﴿and during the hours of the night﴾: he said: the one who prays through the whole night.

Ya'qub ibn Ibrahim narrated to me, saying: Ibn Ulayyah told us, from Abu Raja', who said: I heard al-Hasan recite ﴿and during the hours of the night﴾: he said: from its beginning, its middle, and its end.

Muhammad ibn Sa'd narrated to me, saying: my father told me, saying: my uncle told me, saying: my father told me, from his father, from Ibn Abbas, regarding His saying ﴿and during the hours of the night glorify Him﴾: he said: the hours of the night: the depth of the night.

* *

As for His saying ﴿that you may be pleased﴾:

It means: so that you may be pleased.

The reciters differed in reading this. The majority of the reciters of Medina and Iraq read ﴿la'allaka tarda﴾ with a fatha on the ta'. Asim and al-Kisa'i read it ﴿la'allaka turdha﴾ with a damma on the ta', and this was transmitted from Abu Abd al-Rahman al-Sulami. Those who read it with a fatha seem to have gone to the meaning: God gives you, so that you are pleased with His gift and His reward to you; and the exegetes interpreted it so.

Those who said that:

Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His saying ﴿that you may be pleased﴾: he said: the reward; you are pleased with what God rewards you for that.

Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn told us, saying: Hajjaj told me, from Ibn Jurayj ﴿that you may be pleased﴾: he said: with what you are given. Those who read it with a damma seem to have directed the meaning of the speech to: perhaps God will satisfy you with your worship of Him and your obedience to Him. The correct view on this, in my judgement, is that they are two readings, each of which has been read by scholars among the reciters, and they are two widely transmitted readings in the recitation of the regions, agreeing in meaning and not differing in it, because when God, may He be remembered, pleases someone, there is no doubt that he is pleased, and when he is pleased, God has pleased him; so each of the two indicates the meaning of the other, and whichever of the two a reciter reads, he is correct.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 20, verses 129–130:

The interpretation of His saying, ﴿Had it not been for a word that preceded from your Lord, it would have been inevitable, and a specified term﴾ (129) ﴿So be patient over what they say, and glorify the praise of your Lord before the rising of the sun and before its setting, and during the hours of the night glorify Him, and at the ends of the day, that you may be pleased﴾ (130).

He, may He be remembered, says: ﴿Had it not been for a word that preceded from your Lord﴾, O Muhammad, that everyone for whom He has decreed a term, He will not seize before reaching his term. ﴿And a specified term﴾ means: and an appointed time with your Lord which He has named for them in the Mother of the Book and inscribed in it, which they will surely reach and fulfil. ﴿It would have been inevitable﴾ means: destruction would have been inevitable for them, immediately. It is a verbal noun from the saying of the speaker: "Fulan lazima Fulanan yalazimuhu mulazamatan wa lizaman," meaning: he did not part from him. He placed His saying ﴿it would have been inevitable﴾ before His saying ﴿a specified term﴾. The meaning of the speech is: Had it not been for a word that preceded from your Lord and a specified term, it would have been inevitable, so be patient over what they say.

And the exegetes said things similar to what we have said regarding this.

Those who said that:

Muhammad ibn Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu Asim told us, saying: Isa told us; and al-Harith narrated to me, saying: al-Hasan told us, saying: Warqa' told us, all of them from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His saying ﴿Had it not been for a word that preceded from your Lord, it would have been inevitable, and a specified term﴾: the specified term is the world.

Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid told us, saying: Sa'id told us, from Qatadah, regarding His saying ﴿Had it not been for a word that preceded from your Lord, it would have been inevitable, and a specified term﴾. And this is from the inverted order of speech; He says: Had it not been that a word preceded from your Lord to [[He may mean: had it not been that God's word preceded with the postponement of their punishment to a specified term. It is possible that "ila" (to) was placed in the position of the conjunction waw by a scribe's error.]] a specified term, it would have been inevitable. The specified term is the Hour, for God, may He be exalted, says: ﴿Nay, the Hour is their appointed promise, and the Hour is more calamitous and bitter﴾.

Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His saying ﴿Had it not been for a word that preceded from your Lord, it would have been inevitable, and a specified term﴾: This is inverted and postponed; the meaning is: Had it not been for a word that preceded from your Lord and a specified term, it would have been inevitable.

The exegetes differed regarding the meaning of His saying ﴿it would have been inevitable﴾. Some of them said: its meaning is: it would have been death.

Those who said that:

Ali narrated to me, saying: Abu Salih told me, saying: Mu'awiyah told me, from Ali, from Ibn Abbas, regarding His saying ﴿it would have been inevitable﴾: he says: death.

Others said: its meaning is: it would have been killing.

Those who said that:

Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said ﴿it would have been inevitable﴾, and the inevitability is killing.

* *

As for His saying ﴿So be patient over what they say﴾:

His majestic praise says to His Prophet: Be patient, O Muhammad, over what these deniers of God's signs from your people say to you, that you are a sorcerer, that you are a madman and a poet, and similar sayings. ﴿And glorify the praise of your Lord﴾ means: join your thanksgiving to your Lord, and He said "bi-hamdi rabbika" (with the praise of your Lord), and the meaning is "bi-hamdika rabbaka" (your praise of your Lord), just as you say: "a'jabani darb Zayd" (the striking of Zayd pleased me), meaning "darbi Zaydan" (my striking of Zayd). As for His saying ﴿before the rising of the sun﴾, that is the dawn prayer; ﴿and before its setting﴾, and it is the afternoon prayer; ﴿and during the hours of the night﴾, and they are the hours of the night, its singular being "ini", according to the pattern "hamil", and from it is the saying of al-Mutanakhkhil al-Sa'di:

Sweet and bitter, like the bending of an arrow-shaft is its bitterness,
in every hour of the night that it has passed, it puts on its sandals.

[[(In Lisan: anā) "lani" is the singular of "anā' al-layl", which are its hours; and in the revealed Book: "wa min anā'i al-layli" (and during the hours of the night). The people of language, among them al-Zajjaj, said: "anā' al-layl" are its hours, and its singular is "ini" and "inī"; whoever says "ini" it is like "nahā" and "anhā'"; and whoever says "ini" it is like "ma'ī" and "am'ā'"; al-Hudhali al-Mutanakhkhil said: "al-salik al-thaghra makhshiyyan mawaridahu / bi-kulli ini qadāhu al-layl yantali"*. Al-Azhari said: Ibn al-Anbari narrated it thus, and al-Jawhari recited the verse "Sweet and bitter..." and attributed it also to al-Mutanakhkhil; so either it is the verse he means, or another from a different poem.]]

And by His saying ﴿and during the hours of the night glorify Him﴾ He means the night prayer of 'isha', because it is performed after hours of the night have passed.

* *

As for His saying ﴿and at the ends of the day﴾:

It means the noon and sunset prayers. It was said: "ends of the day" refers to the two prayers that have been mentioned, because the noon prayer is at the end of the first end of the day and at the beginning of the second end of the day, so it lies at both ends; and the third end is the setting of the sun, at which the sunset prayer is performed; therefore it was said "ends" (atraf). It may be said that the two ends of the day are meant. It was also said "atraf", as it was said ﴿your hearts have inclined﴾ in the plural, while two hearts are meant; so the beginning of the second end and the end of the first end would be meant [[In the original: "al-akhir"? This is a scribal error, as is clear from the author's phrasing.]].

And the exegetes said things similar to what we have said regarding this.

Those who said that:

Muhammad ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Rahman told us, saying: Sufyan told us, from Asim, from Ibn Abi Zayd, from Ibn Abbas, regarding ﴿Glorify the praise of your Lord before the rising of the sun and before its setting﴾: he said: the obligatory prayer.

Tamim ibn al-Muntasir narrated to us, saying: Yazid ibn Harun told us, saying: Isma'il ibn Abi Khalid informed us, from Qays ibn Abi Hazim, from Jarir ibn Abd Allah, who said: We were sitting with the Messenger of God (ﷺ), and he looked at the moon on the night of the full moon and said: "Indeed you will see your Lord as you see this, you will not be wronged in seeing Him. So if you are able not to be overcome in a prayer before the rising of the sun and before its setting, then do it." Then he recited ﴿Glorify the praise of your Lord before the rising of the sun and before its setting﴾.

Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn told us, saying: Hajjaj told me, regarding ﴿Glorify the praise of your Lord before the rising of the sun and before its setting﴾: Ibn Jurayj said: the afternoon prayer; and "ends of the day": he said: the obligatory prayer.

Al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Razzaq informed us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah regarding His saying ﴿Glorify the praise of your Lord before the rising of the sun﴾: he said: it is the dawn prayer; ﴿and before its setting﴾: he said: the afternoon prayer; ﴿and during the hours of the night﴾: he said: the sunset and night prayers; ﴿and at the ends of the day﴾: he said: the noon prayer.

Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His saying ﴿and during the hours of the night glorify Him and at the ends of the day﴾: he said: "from the hours of the night": the 'atama (night prayer); "the ends of the day": the sunset and dawn prayers. The phrase ﴿and at the ends of the day﴾ is put in the accusative as a conjunction to His saying ﴿before the rising of the sun﴾, because the meaning is: glorify your Lord with praise at the end of the night and at the ends of the day.

And the exegetes said things similar to what we have said regarding the meaning of ﴿hours of the night﴾.

Those who said that:

Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn told us, saying: Hajjaj told me, from Ibn Jurayj, who said: Ibn Abbas said ﴿and during the hours of the night﴾: he said: the one who prays through the whole night.

Ya'qub ibn Ibrahim narrated to me, saying: Ibn Ulayyah told us, from Abu Raja', who said: I heard al-Hasan recite ﴿and during the hours of the night﴾: he said: from its beginning, its middle, and its end.

Muhammad ibn Sa'd narrated to me, saying: my father told me, saying: my uncle told me, saying: my father told me, from his father, from Ibn Abbas, regarding His saying ﴿and during the hours of the night glorify Him﴾: he said: the hours of the night: the depth of the night.

* *

As for His saying ﴿that you may be pleased﴾:

It means: so that you may be pleased.

The reciters differed in reading this. The majority of the reciters of Medina and Iraq read ﴿la'allaka tarda﴾ with a fatha on the ta'. Asim and al-Kisa'i read it ﴿la'allaka turdha﴾ with a damma on the ta', and this was transmitted from Abu Abd al-Rahman al-Sulami. Those who read it with a fatha seem to have gone to the meaning: God gives you, so that you are pleased with His gift and His reward to you; and the exegetes interpreted it so.

Those who said that:

Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His saying ﴿that you may be pleased﴾: he said: the reward; you are pleased with what God rewards you for that.

Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn told us, saying: Hajjaj told me, from Ibn Jurayj ﴿that you may be pleased﴾: he said: with what you are given. Those who read it with a damma seem to have directed the meaning of the speech to: perhaps God will satisfy you with your worship of Him and your obedience to Him. The correct view on this, in my judgement, is that they are two readings, each of which has been read by scholars among the reciters, and they are two widely transmitted readings in the recitation of the regions, agreeing in meaning and not differing in it, because when God, may He be remembered, pleases someone, there is no doubt that he is pleased, and when he is pleased, God has pleased him; so each of the two indicates the meaning of the other, and whichever of the two a reciter reads, he is correct.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami' al-Bayan) on surah 20, verse 131:

On the interpretation (ta'wil, the explanation of the meaning) of His saying, the Exalted: ﴿And do not extend your eyes toward that with which We have provided some pairs of them, the splendor of the life of this world, that We may test them therein. But the provision of your Lord is better and more enduring﴾ [20:131].

He, may His remembrance be exalted, says to His Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ): Do not look at what We have given to the peers of these people who turn away from the signs of their Lord and their likenesses, as enjoyment in their worldly life, which they enjoy, from the splendor and brightness of the immediate world. ﴿That We may test them therein﴾ means: that We may try them through what We have granted them of that, and examine them. Indeed, that is transient and passing, a delusion and deception that will vanish. ﴿But the provision of your Lord﴾ which He promised to give you in the Hereafter until you are content, and it is His reward given to you, ﴿is better﴾ for you than what We have granted them of the splendor of the life of this world, ﴿and more enduring﴾ means: more lasting, because it has no cessation or end.

It is reported that this verse was revealed to the Messenger of God (ﷺ) because the Messenger of God (ﷺ) sent someone to a Jew to borrow food on credit, and he refused to lend it except against a pledge.

Those who said this:

* Ibn Waki' related to us, saying: My father related to us, from Musa ibn Ubayda, from Yazid ibn Abd Allah ibn Qusayt, from Abu Rafi', who said: The Messenger of God (ﷺ) sent me to a Jew to borrow from him, and he refused to give it except against a pledge. The Messenger of God (ﷺ) was saddened, so God revealed: ﴿And do not extend your eyes toward that with which We have provided some pairs of them, the splendor of the life of this world﴾.

* al-Qasim related to us, saying: al-Husayn related to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Kathir related to us, from Abd Allah ibn Waqid, from Ya'qub ibn Yazid, from Abu Rafi', who said: A guest arrived at the Messenger of God (ﷺ), so he sent me to a Jew in Medina to borrow on credit. I came to him, and he said: "I will not lend it except against a pledge." I informed him of that, and he said: "Indeed, I am trusted among the people of heaven and the people of earth. Take my coat of mail to him." Then it was revealed: ﴿And We have certainly given you seven of the oft-repeated [verses] and the great Qur'an﴾ [15:87], and His saying: ﴿And do not extend your eyes toward that with which We have provided some pairs of them, the splendor of the life of this world﴾ up to His saying: ﴿And the good outcome is for the righteous [in piety]﴾ [20:132].

By His saying ﴿pairs of them﴾ he means men of them, of similar forms. By ﴿the splendor of the life of this world﴾ he means the adornment of the life of this world.

As he [the narrator] said:

* Bishr related to us, saying: Yazid related to us, saying: Sa'id related to us, from Qatada, regarding His saying ﴿the splendor of the life of this world﴾: that is, the adornment of the life of this world. The accusative of "the splendor of the life of this world" is in the status of an exclusive apposition (al-kharuj, i.e., a noun in the accusative standing outside the sentence's main structure) from the pronoun in ﴿We have provided [with it]﴾ (the hā' in bihi). It is like saying: "I passed by him, the noble, the generous," where "the noble, the generous" is accusative by the verb "I passed." Likewise His saying ﴿to what We have provided with it, some pairs of them, the splendor of the life of this world﴾ is accusative by the verb, meaning: We provided them with it as a splendor in the life of this world and an adornment for them therein. Al-Farra' mentioned that some of the Banu Fiqas recited to him:

"After what was in the slope of Safh Kawakib... a pledge of burial in dust and gravel" [[This line is among al-Farra's evidences from some of the Banu Fiqas, as the author said. Kawakib, with a damma on the kaf, is a specific mountain. Rahinat al-rams is one who settled and remained in a place and does not leave it. Al-rams is the grave, or the dust and rocks with which the dead person is covered in his tomb. Al-jandal is the rock. The evidence in the line is that rahina is accusative by the exclusive apposition, as the author said, just as "the splendor of the life of this world" is accusative. The author of Taj al-Arus said: "The kharuj from the leading grammarians is the accusative as an object, and this is the expression of the Basrans, because they say of the object that it is accusative by kharuj, i.e., its removal from the two poles of the predication and its core, and it is like their saying about it: 'a surplus element' (fadla)." Enough. The author meant that rahina is accusative by substitution (badal) from the place of the genitive word (in al-safh), because its place is accusative as an object. Abu al-Baqa' al-Akbari has clarified the aspects of the accusative of "the splendor of life" in his "I'rab al-Qur'an" [2:68] and said that its accusative has several aspects: (First) that it is accusative by a verb omitted, indicated by "We provided," i.e., We made for them the splendor of the life of this world. (Second) that it is a substitution for the place of "with it." (Third) that it is a substitution for "pairs." The meaning is: people of splendor; so the noun was omitted. It is permissible that the pairs were made splendor as an exaggeration. It is not permissible for it to be a qualifier, because it is definite and "pairs" is indefinite. (Fourth) that it is in the sense of dispraise, i.e., I disparage or I mean. (Fifth) that it is a substitution for "what" (ma). Some chose this. Others said: It is not permissible, because His saying ﴿that We may test them therein﴾ is a complement of "We provided," and this would entail separating the complement from the relative pronoun by a foreign element. (Sixth) that it is a circumstantial accusative (hal) from the hā', or from "what," with the tanwin dropped because of two consecutive unvoweled letters, and the genitive "the life" is by substitution. Makki chose this (perhaps Abu al-Haram Makki ibn Rayyan al-Maksini the blind), and there is room for consideration. (Seventh) that it is a specification (tamyiz) for "what," or for the hā' in "with it," reported from al-Farra', and this is an error, because it is definite. Enough.]].

So the accusative of "pledge" is by the verb in His words "after what was in the slope," and there is no doubt that this is weaker in governing the accusative than His saying ﴿We have provided with it, some pairs of them﴾, because the governing element of the noun "pledge" is a genitive particle, not an accusative one.

Those who interpret [the Qur'an] (ahl al-ta'wil) said in accordance with what we have said regarding this.

Those who said this:

* Bishr related to us, saying: Yazid related to us, saying: Sa'id related to us, from Qatada, regarding His saying ﴿that We may test them therein﴾: He said: that We may try them therein. ﴿But the provision of your Lord is better and more enduring﴾ than what We have provided these people from this world.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 20, verse 132:

The interpretation of His, may He be exalted, words: ﴿And enjoin prayer upon your family, and be steadfast in it. We do not ask you for provision; We provide for you, and the good outcome is for righteousness﴾

Almighty God says to His Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ): ﴿And enjoin﴾, O Muhammad, ﴿your family to pray, and be steadfast in it﴾, meaning: and be steadfast in performing it and in observing its prescribed limits, you yourself. ﴿We do not ask you for provision﴾, meaning: We do not ask you for wealth; rather We charge you with a work of your body, and for it We give you a great reward and abundant recompense. He says ﴿We provide for you﴾, meaning: We give you wealth and earn it for you, and We do not ask it of you. As for His words ﴿and the good outcome is for righteousness﴾, He means: the good final outcome of every worker's deeds belongs to the people of piety and fear of God, not to those who fear no punishment from Him and hope for no reward from Him.

Ahl al-ta'wil (the scholars of interpretation) said things similar to what we have said regarding His words ﴿And enjoin prayer upon your family, and be steadfast in it﴾.

Mention of those who said that:

Abu al-Sa'ib narrated to me, saying: Hafs ibn Ghiyath narrated to us, from Hisham ibn 'Urwah, who said: When 'Urwah saw what was in the hands of the rulers, he would enter his house and recite ﴿And do not extend your eyes toward that which We have given to pairs of them as the splendor of the worldly life, that We may test them therein. But the provision of your Lord is better and more lasting. And enjoin prayer upon your family, and be steadfast in it. We do not ask you for provision; We provide for you, and the good outcome is for righteousness﴾, then he would call out: "The prayer, the prayer, may God have mercy on you."

Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: 'Utham narrated to us, from Hisham ibn 'Urwah, from his father, that whenever he saw something of this world, he would come to his family and say: "The prayer," and ﴿And enjoin prayer upon your family, and be steadfast in it. We do not ask you for provision﴾.

Al-'Abbas ibn 'Abd al-'Azim narrated to us, saying: Ja'far ibn 'Awn narrated to us, saying: Hisham ibn Sa'd informed us, from Zayd ibn Aslam, from his father, who said: Among the young servants of 'Umar ibn al-Khattab, I and Yarfa' would spend the night at his place, and he had an hour of the night in which he would pray. When we said that he would not rise at night, he would stand [[Perhaps he means: he would stand (in prayer) standing, i.e., a long standing, and the pronoun in "kana" refers to "Umar," may God be pleased with him.]] for a long time. And whenever he finished praying at night, he would recite this verse: ﴿And enjoin prayer upon your family, and be steadfast in it﴾ ... the verse.

Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Hisham ibn Sa'd informed me, from Zayd ibn Aslam, similarly.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 20, verse 133:

The interpretation of His, may He be exalted, saying: ﴿And they say, "Why does he not bring us a sign from his Lord? Has there not come to them the clear evidence of what is in the former scriptures?"﴾ (20:133)

Allah, may His remembrance be exalted, says: These polytheists, whose characteristics were described in the verses before, said: "Why does Muhammad not bring us a sign from his Lord, as his people's predecessors brought, such as Salih with the she-camel, and Jesus with the raising of the dead and the healing of the blind and the leper?" Allah, may His praise be exalted, says: "Has there not come to them the clarification of what is in the books that came before this Book, concerning the reports of the nations before them, whom We destroyed when they asked for signs and then disbelieved in them when they came to them? [They saw] how We hastened punishment upon them and sent down Our might because of their disbelief in them." He means: "What would assure them that, if a sign came to them, their situation would not be the situation of those [earlier nations]?"

And the people of interpretation (ahl al-ta'wil) said things similar to what we have said on this matter.

Mention of those who said that:

Muhammad ibn Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu Asim narrated to us, saying: Isa narrated to us. And al-Harith narrated to me, saying: al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Warqa' narrated to us, all of them from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His saying ﴿Has there not come to them the clear evidence of what is in the former scriptures?﴾ He said: "The Torah and the Gospel."

Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Juraij, from Mujahid, the like of it.

Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding His saying ﴿Has there not come to them the clear evidence of what is in the former scriptures?﴾ "The books that passed from the nations whose dwellings they walk through."

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 20, verse 134–135:

The interpretation of His saying, ﴿And had We destroyed them with a punishment before it, they would have said, "Our Lord, why did You not send to us a messenger so we could follow Your verses before we were humiliated and disgraced?"﴾ (134)

He, exalted is His remembrance, says: And if We had destroyed these polytheists who deny this Qur'an before We sent it down to them, and before We sent a caller to call them to what We have obligated them to, with a punishment We would send down upon them for their disbelief in Allah, they would have said on the Day of Resurrection, when they came before Us and We intended to punish them: "Our Lord, why did You not send to us a messenger to call us to obeying You, so that we might follow Your verses?" He means: so that we might follow Your proof, Your evidence, and what You send down to him of Your commands and prohibitions, before we were humiliated by Your punishing us and disgraced by it.

As evidence:

Al-Fadl ibn Ishaq narrated to me, saying: Abu Qutaybah Salm ibn Qutaybah narrated to us, from Fudayl, from Marzuq, from ʿAtiyyah al-ʿAwfi, from Abu Saʿid al-Khudri, from the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: "Three will argue with Allah on the Day of Resurrection: the one who died in the interval (of no prophet), the one who was overcome in his intellect, and the young child. The one overcome in his intellect will say: 'You did not give me intellect by which I could benefit.' The one who died in the interval will say: 'No messenger or prophet came to me, and if a messenger or prophet had come to me, I would have been the most obedient of Your creation to You.' And he recited: ﴿Why did You not send to us a messenger?﴾ The young child will say: 'I was a child and did not understand.' He said: Then a fire will be raised for them and it will be said to them: 'Enter it.' He said: So whoever was known in Allah's knowledge to be happy will enter it, and whoever was known in Allah's knowledge to be wretched will hold back from it. Then He will say: 'You disobeyed Me, so how would it be with My messengers had they come to you?'"

* *

The interpretation of His saying, ﴿Say, "Each is waiting, so wait; you will soon know who are the companions of the even path and who is rightly guided."﴾ (135)

He, exalted is His remembrance, says to His Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ): Say, O Muhammad: each of you, O polytheists in Allah, is waiting (mutarabbis), meaning: awaiting to see who will attain success, and to what my affair and yours will lead, and is held in suspense, awaiting the turns of time. So wait (fatarabbasu), meaning: watch and expect. You will soon know (fasa-taʿlamuna), meaning: who are the people of the straight, upright, moderate path that has no crookedness in it, when the command of Allah comes and the Resurrection arises: is it us or you? And who is rightly guided, meaning: and you will then know who is the one guided who is upon the ways of the direct path, not deviating from its course, among us and among you.

Regarding "man" in His saying ﴿fasa-taʿlamuna man aṣḥābu al-ṣirāṭi al-sawiyy﴾ and the second "man" in His saying ﴿wa-man ihtadā﴾, there are two readings: the nominative (raf'), with the verb "taʿlamūn" not operating on them, as He, exalted is His praise, said: ﴿li-naʿlama ayyu al-ḥizbayni aḥṣā﴾ ("that We might know which of the two parties would compute best"); and the accusative (naṣb), with the verb "taʿlamūn" operating on them, as He, exalted is His praise, said: ﴿wa-Allāhu yaʿlamu al-mufsida mina al-muṣliḥ﴾ ("And Allah knows the corrupter from the reformer").

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 20, verse 134–135:

The interpretation of His saying, ﴿And had We destroyed them with a punishment before it, they would have said, "Our Lord, why did You not send to us a messenger so we could follow Your verses before we were humiliated and disgraced?"﴾ (134)

He, exalted is His remembrance, says: And if We had destroyed these polytheists who deny this Qur'an before We sent it down to them, and before We sent a caller to call them to what We have obligated them to, with a punishment We would send down upon them for their disbelief in Allah, they would have said on the Day of Resurrection, when they came before Us and We intended to punish them: "Our Lord, why did You not send to us a messenger to call us to obeying You, so that we might follow Your verses?"
